in writing ‒ the last strategy to support member states in reducing alcohol-related harm was only valid until 2012. excessive alcohol consumption is the second most common cause of lifestyle-related diseases in some member states and alcohol dependence is a risk factor for more than 60 chronic diseases, including alcoholic liver disease, alcoholic pancreatitis and almost all digestive diseases, cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, obesity, fetal alcohol spectrum disorders and neuropsychiatric disorders such as alcohol dependence. the european commission must take a more active approach to this issue and provide advice on reducing alcohol-related problems, as well as supporting the competent authorities in the member states. the european commission must take an active stance on the new eu strategy on alcohol consumption for 2016-2022. member states must urgently step up their efforts to inform citizens about the cultural values of responsible alcohol consumption, the positive health effects of moderate alcohol consumption and its compatibility with a healthy and balanced lifestyle.
in the case of the netherlands, the commission has already adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the european union is a leader in alcohol consumption. this situation is alarming and requires the union, in cooperation with the member states, to prepare a draft strategy to promote the conscious and responsible consumption of alcohol. it is important to focus on the education of adolescents and to establish sufficient awareness of the effects of substances in alcohol on the human body.
in writing. ‒ despite the european commission's indication of the effectiveness of the strategy, the eu alcohol strategy needs further development. it would be a false illusion to try to banish alcohol as a major evil from our lives. alcoholics have been part of european culture for centuries. but its consumption requires attention, self-control. alcohol consumption has a culture, a history and a tradition, but it also poses significant health, public safety and social risks. we need to balance all of these if we want a sustainable european alcohol strategy with real results. i believe that this balance can be achieved by encouraging the consumption of quality alcohol. more economic incentives could be introduced, either by introducing mandatory criteria or by introducing specific taxes. we must instill in the drinking public the principle that quality is more important than quantity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the alcohol strategy. i believe that it is important to combat excessive alcohol consumption. especially should adolescents be kept from drinking alcohol. they need to be educated in this regard. alcoholism has a destructive effect on the development of individuals, families, and thus on society as a whole. i appreciate the fact that alcoholic beverages will be marked with a symbol informing you that alcohol is not suitable for pregnant women.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the alcohol strategy. statistics show that excessive alcohol consumption is the second most common cause of lifestyle-related diseases in some member states and alcohol dependence is a risk factor for more than 60 chronic diseases, including alcoholic liver diseases, almost all digestive diseases, cancer, diabetes, obesity, heart disease and many neuropsychiatric disorders. excessive alcohol use kills 6% of people every year, with 25% of those dying between the ages of 20 and 39. excessive drinking among young people is becoming commonplace. alcohol use problems are related to many factors, such as socioeconomic status, cultural background, parental and peer pressure, family and school upbringing, revenge, and education. . . . the call to the commission to draw up a new strategy on alcohol consumption must therefore be drawn up in cooperation with the individual member states and must be aimed at preventing, reprimanding and educating young people about the particularly harmful effects of alcohol on young people's bodies, and the social and health consequences for the individual, the family and society.
in writing. ‒ health protection should be the foundation of every society. however, in the fight against alcoholism, i place particular emphasis on prevention, raising awareness of the consequences and risks associated with excessive alcohol consumption, and more coverage of this topic in the education of children, young people and adults.
in writing. ‒ although the number of babies born with fetal alcohol syndrome is increasing every year, the issue has not yet received the attention it deserves. for years, many experts have warned that drinking alcohol during pregnancy can have devastating effects on the unborn child. even a small amount can seriously impair a child's development and manifest itself in physical and mental disabilities. but unlike other disabilities, fetal alcohol syndrome is preventable. i am pleased that the resolution on the alcohol strategy we adopted also touches on this topic and calls on the member states and the commission, as well as all stakeholders, to examine and strengthen awareness-raising campaigns on the harmful effects of alcohol consumption, in particular on pregnant women, and on the impact of alcohol on the unborn child. one effective campaign is certainly the use of pictograms to warn of these risks on alcoholic beverages. i believe that good vengeance can save many children from permanent and serious health damage.

in writing ‒ the recent tragic events in the mediterranean have prompted a review of the european union's migration and asylum policy. italy has been particularly hard hit by the mass influx of migrants, with 170,000 arriving on its shores last year alone. managing such an influx of asylum seekers imposes a burden on the security and rescue forces, administration and other significant costs associated with providing assistance to these persons. it is necessary for the commission to develop a strategy on migration and asylum policy that responds to events in the mediterranean while encouraging all local and international institutions to put in place political, economic and anti-corruption measures that will stop the unwanted migration of the population.
in writing. ‒ the refugees from africa and the middle east need practical help, not sympathy and pity. from a humanitarian point of view, we are clearly obliged to provide urgent assistance to those who are fighting for their lives in the waters of the mediterranean. at the same time, we must not forget the complex and long-term solutions offered by much more effective development aid. more effective development aid to the countries of origin of migrants means tackling the root of the problem. it allows people to stay to live and work in their home countries, without disrupting family and social ties and without exposing themselves to the often very precarious conditions in the host countries, whose language and culture they do not know. as far as the reception of refugees in the eu is concerned, it is not rational, nor economically and socially viable, to consider refugees from all over the world en masse. we cannot be responsible for the personal decision of individuals who leave their own country with knowledge of the risk. i would remind you that public officials have a primary duty to their own citizens, who must be protected from the negative consequences of endangering their safety, health or even their lives. in conclusion, i strongly support and expect the speedy delivery of humanitarian aid and the concrete follow-up to it.
in writing. the events in syria, libya and other african countries, the result of the conflict, the fact that the mediterranean is burying hundreds of people almost every day, have forced the representatives of the european council to take urgent action to prevent similar situations. increasing the budget is not the panacea and other solutions will have to be found, in particular to prevent organised smuggling gangs from making millions off the misery of the people. i consider the adoption of this resolution to be urgent and it is high time that we make every effort to save the lives of people in danger and to prevent further loss of life at sea. in addition to the tasks that await frontex, i expect measures to be taken to ensure a common european asylum system, and i also expect a review of the overall strategy of cooperation with third countries to tackle the root causes of migration. the situation in the mediterranean leaves no one indifferent, which is why i am pleased that the commission's priorities for 2015 include addressing the issue of migrants, even though it was too late yesterday.
in writing. ‒ to prevent similar tragedies, it is important that the european union not only address the consequences of similar tragedies, but also address their causes. it is essential to better manage development aid and to use it to improve the living standards of the countries from which the largest number of refugees and asylum seekers arrive in the eu. only in this way will we be able to tackle the problems of eu migration and asylum policy in a systematic way.

in writing. albania a small country of less than 3 million people, it has made remarkable progress towards eu accession in recent times. it was therefore granted candidate country status in june 2014. however, there are still areas where albania needs to take major steps these are mainly judicial reform, the fight against corruption and organised crime. the current ongoing polarization of political forces in the country and the persistence of corruption, which also affects the judiciary, may jeopardise albania's integration efforts, thus undermining citizens' trust in a fair judicial system. the business environment and the drive for a functioning market economy have improved in recent times, but the government must continue to address shortcomings in treaty and rule of law enforcement and combat the informal economy. the albanian people will have to make sacrifices and suffer in the process of integration in the various measures taken by the government, but they will surely understand that this is necessary for albania to be an equal member of the eu in the future.
in writing. ‒ i am confident that albania will continue to implement reforms that will bring it closer to the eu. in addition to democratising society, fighting corruption and making public administration more efficient, it is essential to establish a constructive and sustainable political dialogue and to step up albania's cooperation with the european union.

last week, sándor lámfalussy, who many in this room know as alexander lámfalussy, and rightly considered the father of the euro, passed away. he was a hungarian, one of the important personalities that the hungarian nation gave to the democratic world. born in 1929 in kaposvár, hungary, he emigrated in 1949 from the communist dictatorship. he graduated in economics from the catholic university of leuven in 1953, after which he was a manager in several major banks. from 1994 to 1997, he was the first president of the european monetary institute (emi), based in frankfurt. under his leadership, the institute prepared the transition to the euro and coordinated the monetary policies of the eu member states. he was the recipient of many awards, and after my lecture at the hungarian academy of sciences in budapest 10 years ago, he came to me, put his hand on my shoulder and said, "hold on, my son, you're going to slovakia too!" which meant that we were on the horizon of his morally based worldview, not hungarians living in hungary.

in writing. ‒ the the correct interpretation and use of benchmarks allows the internal market to function effectively. for their consistent and correct application, it is essential that they are not affected by conflicts of interest, that they reflect the economic reality they are intended to measure and that they are used in an appropriate manner. effective control mechanisms should be put in place to prevent their misuse and to highlight the illegality and criminality of such conduct. administrators of benchmarks shall be required to put in place measures and mechanisms to enhance confidence in the integrity of benchmarks and to prevent any manipulation of benchmarks.

in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that health systems in individual member states have undergone significant reforms in recent years and governments are striving to provide citizens with better healthcare. however, 8-12% of patients hospitalised in the european union experienced adverse events during the provision of healthcare. approximately 4.1 million patients in the european union contract hospital-acquired infections each year and at least 37 000 die as a result, which is a very alarming figure. it is very unfortunate that we have reached a situation where it is becoming increasingly clear that the level of care and safety for patients is often limited by various austerity measures and horizontal cuts, which is unacceptable because the protection of human life and health must be the absolute priority and all economic indicators must be sidelined in this case. healthcare policies should not be subject to austerity measures and cuts, and relevant institutions should provide patients with the highest possible level of safety and protection of human life.
in writing. ‒ the antimicrobial resistance poses a serious threat to humanity and has a negative impact on public health. it endangers the lives and health of people and animals, and it increases the demand for health funding. the bulk use of medicines, especially antibiotics, has the effect of reducing their effectiveness, causing the spread of microbes and bacteria. in order to slow down the development and limit the spread of bacteria containing antimicrobial resistance genes, it is necessary that the commission, in cooperation with the member states and the professional bodies, take all measures to raise awareness among the public and among healthcare professionals themselves. measures must aim at the responsible and correct use of antimicrobials, which should lead to a reduction of the risks to human health and at the same time to a positive impact on public finances.
in writing. ‒ every year, 4.1 million patients are infected in healthcare across europe and 37 000 unfortunately die. together with the number of problems caused by errors in hospitals, this accounts for 8-12% of patients treated in the eu. it is sad that only a fraction of member states have implemented the council's proposals, despite the fact that 30 to 40% of problems are caused by errors and 20 to 30% of infections could have been prevented. we have to change that. i believe it is important that member states implement the council's innovations, especially in the areas of patient rights, infection prevention and training of health workers. it is essential to continue work on the establishment of a central european classification system and on european guidelines in the field of patient safety. safe healthcare is the foundation of a well-functioning health system and every effort should be made to ensure that safety is the foundation of public health structures in the union.
in writing. ‒ it is estimated that by 2050, 10 million people worldwide will die each year as a result of the emergence of new superbugs resistant to all antibiotics. the emergency situation requires adequate solutions. that is why i voted for the resolution on safer healthcare in europe.
in writing. i supported the report on safer healthcare because i consider patient safety and the fight against drug resistance to be a very important role for the eu as a whole and for the member states individually. patient safety, as well as the right of the patient not to suffer harm as a result of the provision of healthcare, must be a decisive element in the quality of healthcare provision. according to available data, up to 8-12% of eu hospitalized patients will suffer an injury or adverse event, including healthcare-associated infections, many of which could have been prevented. and that's three million people with inaccurate and not always up-to-date data collections from health care providers. progress in patient safety is uneven across member states. i am glad that slovakia is in the group of countries with safer health care at 4 13%. paradoxically, many patients are also endangered by the doctors themselves, who prescribe antibiotics for many diseases (e.g. viral diseases, for which antibiotics have no effect), thus making patients resistant to common antimicrobials. the self-medication of patients with antibiotics should also be strictly prohibited, and this should be prevented by vigorous reprisals against medical personnel, the media and possibly a pan-european awareness campaign.

in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the backbone of the european economy, an important driver of economic growth and job creation. the sectors involved in green growth offer significant economic and ecological benefits to smes in the union, and these benefits could increase in the coming years. this economic growth may be accompanied by environmental sustainability, which is one of the key challenges of the coming decades. the green economy holds a lot of potential for smes, but at the moment these opportunities are only partially exploited. there is still a long way to go to make smes' production processes, business practices and services greener. the eu institutions and national decision-makers need to find a solution that not only reduces the burden on smes, but also effectively promotes the creation of greener businesses with equal opportunities in all member states. specific initiatives are needed to encourage smes at member state level to extend the benefits of green growth. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ to cope with the consequences of the global economic and financial crisis, the european union must support small and medium-sized enterprises in every possible way, since they are the most active part of the european economy and create countless jobs. the green growth sector has the potential to grow continuously and actively in the coming years, and it is therefore important that we fully realise the potential of the green economy. smes must be actively involved in the greening of the products they produce, as well as of production processes, business practices and services. the european commission should encourage this effort in every possible way, recognising the benefits of green growth. the european commission should actively contribute to the simplification of the differences in the national systems of the member states, thus moving towards a more uniform set of measures. it is therefore clear from recent developments that there is room for a rather significant ecological potential, and it is very important that we are able to exploit this potential to the maximum extent possible and that it benefits smes across the european union.
in writing. ‒ smes account for around 99% of all european businesses and provide some 75 million jobs, making them a fundamental pillar of the european union's economy. to ensure their sustainable and inclusive growth, it is essential to promote, in a targeted and conscious manner, the increasing implementation of a green economy that uses resources efficiently. it is necessary for member states, in cooperation with the european commission, to seek tools to support the business and legal environment in terms of access to project financing, public procurement and other public policy tools that enable smes to take advantage of environmental challenges for the benefit of economic growth.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on green growth opportunities for smes. i agree with the ecr's position that the green growth sector provides major economic and environmental benefits to smes in the eu and is expected to grow significantly in the coming years, based on the fact that this economic growth can be linked to environmental sustainability. i consider smes to be an important driver of economic growth and job creation in all eu countries.
in writing. smes form the backbone of the european economy, accounting for around 99% of all european enterprises and providing some 75 million jobs. supporting smes at eu level, but also at member state level, to have easier access to finance is therefore essential for the adoption of greener technologies and for investments in sustainable business practices. it is important that local and regional authorities provide smes with adequate information and analyses of production sectors and structures within which smes can progress with green growth. on the eu institutions' side, i consider it important to remove the obstacles that prevent the mobilisation of funds, while minimising the administrative burden for smes. the eu programmes are not currently making a significant contribution to green innovation and the circular economy, so the commission needs to better target funding from cosme and horizon 2020 programmes to the development of green and innovative solutions by smes.
in writing. ‒ to ensure the sustainability and competitiveness of european economies, it is important to focus on resource efficiency and energy efficiency. i would like to stress that smes account for approximately 99% of all european enterprises and employ some 75 million workers. to create a sustainable environment, it is necessary to simplify access to finance for businesses, to support people in setting up businesses, to simplify the rules for entrepreneurship and to reduce the administrative burden. one tool that can motivate people to start a business is the adoption of the single-member company directive, which allows companies to be set up in the eu through online registration and with a minimum capital of eur 1. the european union should take all steps to ensure that this directive is adopted.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the proposal because i do not agree with the visions and proposals of the report submitted. the report presented shows a fundamental misunderstanding of how the market works, how economic growth and job creation are generated. the report thus points out how the redistribution of taxpayers' money will help growth or job creation, but does not show that the jobs and growth thus achieved are achieved only at the expense of potentially even more growth and employment, or at the expense of creating more sustainable growth and employment.

in writing. ‒ i support the legislative resolution of the rapporteur approving the council position for the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on insolvency proceedings. one of the key objectives of the proposed insolvency regulation is to move away from the traditional liquidation approach towards a second chance approach for businesses and entrepreneurs in financial difficulty in cross-border insolvency proceedings. the council's position also contains new rules aimed at preventing the abuse of the jurisdiction clause. also, in order to improve the provision of relevant and timely information to creditors and the courts involved and to avoid the initiation of parallel insolvency proceedings, the regulation imposes an obligation on member states to set up insolvency registers. national registers will have to be linked and accessible via the european e-justice portal in full compliance with european data protection legislation. the regulation should also contain specific provisions on cooperation and communication between courts and insolvency practitioners involved in the insolvency of members of groups of companies.
written ‒ i did not support the proposal because, while it introduces some minor changes that may increase the efficiency of insolvency proceedings, it also introduces one significant change that may substantially reduce the responsible behaviour of debtors. this is a change in the approach to insolvency proceedings, whereby, if certain conditions are met, entrepreneurs can be given a 'second chance' to survive as 'healthy firms'. however, this approach significantly increases the moral hazard, as debtors will be aware that they will not be fully liable for any default. as such a 'second chance' must necessarily be granted to the detriment of the interests of the creditors, it can be assumed that this will increase the prices of the loans, since the creditors will have to take into account a higher risk of losing money.

in writing. ‒ a historic opportunity for the un to examine whether the eu is properly implementing the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the european parliament also takes the opportunity to send a reply to the un on its own behalf in the form of an adopted resolution, detailing what the institution is doing for people with disabilities. the ep resolution calls on the three eu member states that have not yet ratified the convention to do so as soon as possible, and those that have already done so - including the eu itself - to speed up the implementation of the convention. it also urged the european commission to formally involve parliament in a constructive dialogue with the un and to produce the long-awaited european accessibility legislation. the eu's framework cooperation to monitor the implementation of the convention, of which the ep is a member, needs resources to function effectively. following the un final report, parliament's empl, libe and peti committees will shortly produce a joint report. this institutional cooperation at international level for the rights of persons with disabilities can, for example, serve as a basis for similar actions for the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities, who also require greater legal protection and attention than national minorities. i voted in favour of the adoption of the motion because it promotes the effective implementation of the un convention.
in writing. ‒ the european union fully supports and promotes the active inclusion and full participation of people with disabilities in society. it should be remembered that disability is a matter of rights, not discretion. in 2010, the european commission adopted a european disability strategy for the years 2010 to 2020. the main objectives of this strategy include, inter alia, accessibility, participation, equality, employment, education and training, social protection, health and external relations.
in writing. ‒ the european union has ratified and become a party to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. it has been signed by all 28 member states and ratified by 25. the eu has thus committed itself to building a barrier-free europe for 80 million people with different forms of disability by 2020. despite the convention entering into force in 2011, its content is not being implemented as expected and persons with disabilities continue to face various forms of discrimination compared to other persons. it is therefore necessary to develop analyses in cooperation with organisations representing disabled people, which give a realistic assessment of the situation regarding the treatment of the rights of disabled citizens. i encourage the rapid development and submission of measures that will lead to the effective removal of barriers and the immediate fulfilment of the convention's obligations.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on the resolution on the list of subjects adopted by the united nations committee on the rights of persons with disabilities in relation to the initial report of the european union. this resolution contains many important proposals which i consider very useful. at the same time, however, it refers to the non-adoption of an anti-discrimination directive, which in its current form carries the risk of endangering contractual freedom and of dangerously vague and very broad interpretation, which could in turn lead to legal uncertainty and also to restrictions on civil rights and freedoms.
in writing. the principles of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities point the way to ensuring that all persons with disabilities can enjoy their human rights, and focus on providing the necessary protection and assistance to families, which should contribute to enabling persons with disabilities to fully and equally exercise their rights. the committee on petitions receives petitions every year which point to discrimination on the grounds of disability in access to employment, self-employment, public services and education. therefore, eu funding should also be used to support accessibility and e-accessibility for persons with disabilities, to support the transition from institutional to community-based care, to develop quality social and health services and to invest in capacity building of organisations representing persons with disabilities. in the development of future eu policies and legislation, it is necessary to ensure that persons with disabilities have equal rights and obligations in the labour market, in the use of services, in leisure activities and in personal life.
in writing. ‒ there are more than 80 million people with disabilities in the european union who, unlike healthy citizens, cannot enjoy the freedoms on which the european union is built. unfortunately, it will be a long time before we can say that the whole old continent is really capable of taking care of the most vulnerable. the union should lead by example in respecting the obligations arising from the convention and promote barrier-free access not only within individual member states but also across borders. barriers should also not be in place to access to healthcare for the disabled. the moment we remove all these barriers, we will be able to say that the right to freedom of movement is truly a privilege for all.

‒ the kyoto protocol to the 1997 un framework convention on climate change has set itself the goal of reducing emissions. the eu ratified the protocol in 2002 and under the protocol its member states were responsible for reducing their collective greenhouse gas emissions by 8% from 1990 levels in the first period 2008 to 2012. subsequently, in 2012, the council agreed and proposed that the eu reduce emissions by 20% (from 1990 levels). the doha amendment established the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, ending on 31 december 2020, where the eu and iceland committed to limit their average annual emissions by 2020 to 80% of the 1990 base year.
in writing ‒ the doha addendum commits the european union, its member states and iceland to reduce their average annual greenhouse gas emissions by 20% from the base year 1990 over the period 2013 to 2020. this commitment is based on the european legal framework for climate and energy policy until 2020. the proposal does not change the objectives or commitments of member states under the 2009 climate and energy package legislation, thus respecting the principle that individual member states' commitments to reduce their emissions in the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol do not exceed their commitments contained in the eu legislation making up the package.
‒ the kyoto protocol, signed in 1997, commits the eu and its member states to reducing their collective greenhouse gas emissions by 8% compared to 1990 levels in the first period (2008 2012). in 2012, the council introduced the second commitment period (2013 2020) of the kyoto protocol in the doha addendum, where it proposed a joint qualified commitment for the eu, the member states and iceland to reduce by 20% compared to 1990, and thus the parties committed to reduce emissions by 80% compared to 1990. the doha amendment also introduced three amendments to the text of the kyoto protocol, concerning the inclusion of a new gas (nitrous fluoride), an ambition mechanism allowing a party to adjust the commitment by increasing its ambition, and provisions preventing emissions from rising above the level of the first commitment period in the second commitment period. i agree that in order to achieve effective adoption and implementation of the doha annex before the start of the unfccc conference in paris at the end of 2015, it is necessary for member states to ratify the annex by the third quarter of 2015 at the latest.
in writing. ‒ as we all know, the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, covering the period from 1 january 2013 to 31 december 2020, entered into force in 2012 as a result of the doha climate conference. for that phase, we set a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 20% compared to the reference year (which is the base year 1990 for most states that have ratified the kyoto protocol). i'm convinced that the only way this is going to happen is if we can somehow get the u.s. and china to take this commitment seriously. we need to put our economic and diplomatic efforts into action to address climate change as a truly global issue. i think that's the only way we can achieve our goal of limiting global warming to two degrees celsius. at the level of member states, we should not delay but urgently ratify the doha amendment before the paris conference of the unfccc in november 2015.
‒ in 2002, when the european union ratified the kyoto protocol, it agreed to implement the emission commitment jointly, which applies to all member states, including the slovak republic. when voting on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol, which provides for a reduction of emissions below 20% of 1990 levels, i voted in favour of this resolution, as, on the basis of the council's position, the member states themselves adopted the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol at the doha conference in 2012.
‒ i supported the ep resolution on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the doha addendum to the kyoto protocol to the un framework convention on climate change and the joint fulfilment of the commitments thereunder. the kyoto protocol is a key contribution to addressing global climate change. the ratification decision to conclude the doha addendum to the kyoto protocol is a good strong signal about the role of the eu and its member states in addressing climate change. the doha amendment was adopted at the doha conference in december 2012, where the 192 parties to the kyoto protocol adopted an amendment to the protocol, and it sets out a second commitment period whereby the eu, its member states and iceland commit to limit their average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the years 2013 2020 to 80% of their base year 1990 emissions. the doha amendment also introduces further changes to the text of the kyoto protocol the inclusion of a new gas, nitrous fluoride, a simplified procedure allowing for adjustments to the greenhouse gas reduction commitment and preventing emissions from rising above the average of previous years.
in writing, ‒ i welcome this proposal from the commission. i regret that the commitments of the kyoto protocol are being made by the majority of eu countries, and not by the ones that pollute our land the most. the eu should use all possible political, diplomatic and economic instruments to force these countries to sign a binding international agreement. the ratification decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and the joint fulfilment of commitments by the european union can thus contribute to addressing climate change at international level.
‒ the agreement between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on its participation in the second period of the kyoto protocol will send a signal about the joint european efforts to address climate change at international level. we welcome the eu's position, which has become crucial, especially in international climate change negotiations. we therefore consider it important that the council decision on the doha annex and iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments be ratified simultaneously and without undue delay.
‒ article 4 of the kyoto protocol allows the parties to fulfil their commitments jointly. in a joint statement, the eu and its member states expressed their intention to meet their emission reduction targets jointly in the second commitment period, with the extension of the joint fulfilment to iceland, following its formal request of june 2009.
‒ the kyoto protocol entered into force in february 2005 and aims to commit emissions reductions in the first period (2008 2012). the eu and its member states have ratified the convention and committed to reducing emissions by 8% compared with 1990 levels. iceland, which is not an eu member state but has also ratified the kyoto protocol, has also committed to reducing emissions at the same level. in 2012, the doha climate change conference adopted an addendum to the kyoto protocol extending the emissions reduction period to 2020 and agreeing to a gradual reduction of emissions to 80% of 1990 levels. as iceland is not an eu member state, the council decision authorises an agreement between the eu and its member states and between the eu and iceland, to facilitate the participation of iceland and to create a binding obligation towards the eu. for the purpose of the entry into force of this agreement, i agree that the council decision on the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments under this convention must be ratified in parallel, in good time before the start of the unfccc conference in paris, which will take place at the end of 2015.
in writing. ‒ i support iceland's participation in the second commitment phase of the kyoto protocol. i believe that by joining forces we will be able to achieve the objectives set for the stages ahead. on the other hand, i also think it's important to work with other major powers, like china, the united states, which are the biggest emitters.
‒ although iceland is not a member state of the european union, it participates in the european union emissions trading system and has therefore decided to fulfil its commitment to the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and to participate in joint fulfilment with the european union, which is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

in writing ‒ i appreciate iceland's proactive approach to environmental issues and to tackling climate change. although not an eu member state, iceland is still participating in the eu ets and intends to fulfil its commitment in the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol together with the eu and its member states. it is therefore necessary that the rights and obligations applicable to member states in the joint implementation also apply to iceland, through eu legislation and a new agreement between the eu, all member states and iceland.
in writing. ‒ as the rapporteur for the report, i consider it important that croatia accede to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union of 29 may 2000 and therefore voted in favour of the recommendation. accession will complete croatia's membership of the eu. the purpose of the convention is to promote mutual assistance in criminal matters between the competent authorities of the member states, including police, customs or judicial authorities, with a view to more effective and rapid cooperation in criminal matters. in a union without borders, where people, goods, services and capital can move freely, crime is no longer bound by national borders. crime cannot be prosecuted at the national level. only effective cooperation at european level can bring about the desired results. this requires mutual trust, as law enforcement has traditionally been a national competence and the competent authorities of one member state are reluctant to share information with the authorities of another member state. the convention aims to do just that by encouraging and promoting mutual assistance and trust between member states, which is one of the cornerstones of effective judicial cooperation. it also covers certain forms of mutual legal assistance, such as the setting up of joint investigation teams, and covert investigations. i hope that croatia's accession will bring positive progress in the efficiency of european law enforcement.
‒ the accession of croatia to the eu has also facilitated its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states under article 34 of the treaty on european union. however, the european commission recommendation contains an error concerning the date of entry into force of the convention between croatia and the member states and such provisions could lead to unclear procedures.
in writing ‒ the recommendation is based on the act of accession of croatia. the aim is to make the necessary adjustments required by the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report and croatia's accession to this very important convention. it is good to see that croatia, as the newest member of the eu, is gradually closing all the accession procedures and joining the conventions already adopted and operated by the other member states. this is the way forward, so that croatian eu citizens can make the most of their country's eu membership and eu achievements. i hope that citizens will soon experience the benefits of solidarity and cooperation in their daily lives.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation to croatia to accede to the 1997 convention on the fight against corruption. although croatia's accession to the convention may be considered a formality, it is of paramount importance as it completes its accession to the union and ultimately contributes to a better functioning european union. as the rapporteur of the report, i consider it extremely important that croatia accedes to the convention, as the convention on the fight against corruption involving eu officials and officials of the member states of the european union makes the union accountable to its citizens. under the agreement, member states are to take all necessary measures to ensure that both passive and active corruption are criminalised. this is the only way to ensure that abuses of power are effectively tackled. it should be regarded as an offence not only to promise or give an official any advantage, that is to say direct, active corruption, but also to ask for or accept any advantage, whether national or of a european institution, in order to take or not to take a measure within its competence or in the exercise of its competence in breach of its official duties. moreover, since crime in the schengen eu does not stop at the national border, the convention calls on member states to cooperate when anti-corruption proceedings affect at least two member states, whether in the form of cooperation in investigations, criminal proceedings or the enforcement of sentences.

in writing ‒ the european union should have an interest in maintaining constructive relations over the long term, aimed at addressing common global challenges, such as the fight against terrorism and organised crime, but also those related to climate change and the development of new technologies. unfortunately, the russian federation has been actively using hybrid warfare in recent months, deliberately blurring the line between military/paramilitary activities and political action. in addition, it has taken deliberate actions aimed at destabilising neighbouring countries, contrary to the spirit of good neighbourly relations and in breach of international law, rules and norms. the eu is interested in improving relations with the russian federation, but it is its duty to use all means to prevent such actions by the russian federation.
in writing ‒ relations between the european union and the russian federation are at their most difficult. they are affected by a complex geopolitical situation which ultimately affects and harms the economy and economic interests of both sides. this adverse situation has repercussions not only for the russian federation and its population, but also for individual member states and the eu. we need to look for what unites us and work together to remove barriers. the current complicated state of eu-russia relations calls for intensified diplomatic activity, increased communication and enhanced objective information exchange. the mere use of economic sanctions without rational communication will hardly reverse the current state of affairs.
in writing ‒ since the beginning of the conflict in ukraine, the positions of the russian federation and the european union have diverged and even contradicted each other, as russia is suspected of being directly or indirectly involved in the unrest in eastern ukraine, the annexation of the crimean peninsula and the undermining of the sovereignty of independent states that were formerly part of the soviet union. such behaviour destabilises the eu's neighbours and is contrary to international law, as it threatens peace between independent countries. the eu cannot therefore currently take the russian side as a trusted partner, as it is acting in breach of democratic principles. russia has even recently been challenging the democratic regime and the rule of law. relations with the russian federation, which is moving away from the values espoused by the eu, therefore need to be reassessed accordingly. the repair and restoration of strategic relations is possible if the russian side respects the minsk agreements, stops destroying ukraine's internal infrastructure and accepts the independence and sovereignty of this state.

in writing ‒ the drive to increase economic growth and raise the living standards of the population increases demand for raw materials and energy and their resources. the european union's energy security thus becomes the key to its economic growth, competitiveness and strong political and economic standing. this requires, in particular in the context of the current geopolitical challenges, that the eu and its member states ensure a common energy policy as an integral part of both the eu's internal and external policies. the energy security strategy emphasises the search for ways to reduce energy demand and increase the share of domestically produced energy and the development of new energy technologies, requiring a well-functioning energy market.
in writing ‒ the energy security of the european union plays a key role in affirming europe's strong political and economic position. as the european commission already outlined the main challenges in the energy security sector in may 2014, political impetus from the european parliament is now needed to outline a framework for improved energy security. although the situation has improved compared to the past, the eu is still forced to import 53% of its total energy consumption. it is therefore necessary to implement a long-term strategy setting out strategic objectives with regard to europe's energy security, based on key pillars for reducing energy demand. as energy security issues are often addressed at member state level, regardless of the interdependence between member states, i support the idea of a single european energy security for a more competitive european union and a well-functioning internal energy market. as for the question of russia's credibility as a trading partner, it is clear that it uses energy for political purposes. i therefore support the idea that member states should adopt a uniform approach to foreign suppliers.

in writing. the european union's immigration policy needs to be changed. the member states' representatives have to find a way of combining the need for security, mutual solidarity and humanitarian values, which are one of the pillars of our civilisation. solutions must not be taken on the spur of the moment, but must be systematic and permanent. the problem of immigration must be tackled comprehensively and preventively. firstly, there is a need to better coordinate actions to protect the eu's coasts and also to improve cooperation in the search for and arrest of those who profit from human misery. the annual profits from such crime are estimated at up to eur 20 billion, and this money is often mined in europe. first, the causes, not the consequences, of this situation must be addressed. the causes must be addressed where they originate, in the countries of origin of the migrants. the european institutions and individual member states should therefore consider a common strategy to stop illegal migrants in their countries of origin. the development programmes for the countries concerned should serve this purpose. the emerging energy union can also help, as the north africa and middle east region is expected to be one of the sources from which the eu will draw oil and gas in increasing numbers. as economic levels improve, one of the reasons for mass emigration will also disappear.

in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation responds to the reduced growth of investment in the european union, which has fallen by 15% compared to 2007 as a result of the financial and economic crisis. this has a negative impact on economic growth, employment and competitiveness. the proposed regulation on the european fund for strategic investments aims to establish a legal framework and budgetary means to support investments and subsequently to adopt measures to enhance the regulatory environment and remove obstacles that hinder investments. the beneficiaries will be mainly small and medium-sized enterprises, which will be able to create new jobs and stimulate the economic market by drawing on efsi financing. at the same time, a european investment advisory hub will be established to act as a single technical advisory hub for the financing of european union projects. investments must support the development of infrastructure, education, health, research, development, information and communication technologies and innovation, the spread of renewable energy and energy efficiency, infrastructure projects in the areas of environment, natural resources, urban development and social sphere.

in writing. ‒ the on the basis of the evaluation of the common agricultural policy in 2003, member states agreed to end the quota system for milk and milk products by 31 march 2015. the end of quotas presents new challenges and opportunities for the milk and milk products sector. overall, the sector has a positive outlook on the internal market, but also on the world market, in particular due to the high demand from fast-developing economies. nevertheless, in recent months, the decline in demand on external markets, the volatility of world prices and the russian embargo have put pressure on the sector and created enormous downward pressure on prices. the current eu crisis measures and instruments are unfortunately not tailored to the realities of modern dairy farming. it is therefore our duty to adopt, and above all to ensure the implementation of, measures to promote a competitive and sustainable milk and milk products sector.
in writing. ‒ small milk producers, including those in slovakia, are currently facing pressure from several quarters. in slovakia, this is mainly due to the abolition of quotas and embargoes by russia. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution on the prospects for the eu milk sector. the resolution points out that the surplus of dairy products from some member states creates a major imbalance on the domestic markets, resulting in a sharp fall in prices and a loss of competitiveness for local small producers. the resolution calls on the commission to take urgent action to create new financing possibilities for the member states through the european investment bank, the guarantee fund and the revolving fund.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that, in view of the expiry of milk quotas on 31 march 2015 and the current situation in the production of milk and milk products, it is necessary to review the implementation of the milk package, which should apply until 30 june 2020. in this context, i consider it extremely important that the commission should prepare new ways of supporting the dairy industry, which is becoming increasingly unstable worldwide. i regret to say that in my home country of slovakia, the milk sector is also in crisis, and i hope that this crisis will not be like the one in 2008 2009, when there was a significant drop in purchase prices in slovakia and dozens of companies stopped primary milk production. although only a very short time had passed since the abolition of quotas, as in europe, the price, which caused the imbalance in the market, became the only regulatory instrument on the market in slovakia. i expect the commission, in cooperation with the member states and the dairy industry stakeholders, to develop effective and appropriate instruments to safeguard against sudden and significant falls in milk prices.
in writing. ‒ the resolution assesses the impact of the measures included in the milk package so far, including the cancellation of milk quotas for small producers and the embargo imposed by russia on imports of our dairy products. i voted in favour of the report because it contains a number of useful recommendations, the implementation of which can help to strengthen the dairy industry: to set raw milk prices more fairly, to increase exports of products to new foreign markets and to create jobs.

rapporteur.– mr president, the european union needs a more strategic, ambitious and forward-looking neighbourhood policy. setting this policy right is currently one of the greatest challenges in the eu’s external relations. it is in our interest to have a stable, secure, prosperous and democratic neighbourhood. i call therefore in my report for us to go back to basics, to reinforce the creation of an area of prosperity, stability and good neighbourliness. we are facing new challenges in our neighbourhood: the crisis in ukraine, developments in the southern and eastern neighbourhood, migration, terrorism, energy security. in a situation like that, the eu needs to be able to react promptly to changing realities. more than ever, we need a politically- driven neighbourhood policy. the eu needs to show leadership and vision. we need to be aware of the diversity of our neighbourhood but, at the same time, keep the single policy framework. it is understandable that countries in our neighbourhood have different ambitions and expectations. we need to be ready to differentiate between the partners but expect results in the shape of reforms from those who show a clear interest in closer relations with the eu. faced with numerous crises, we need to use our foreign policy instruments in a more flexible way. we should be able to mobilise sufficient resources through our financing instruments. i call, therefore, for this policy review to be reflected in the mid-term review of the external financing instruments. more importantly, our know-how may often be more important than money. we need to look at the possibility of using it more efficiently in processes of state-building, transformation, democratisation or conflict resolution. support for democracy, human rights and the rule of law needs to stay at the heart of the reviewed policy. we need to strengthen partnership with the societies in neighbourhood countries and promote the values which are at the core of the union. the reviewed policy needs to include numerous aspects of security. therefore, i propose including support for capacity-building and state structures able to deal with the security threats in countries affected. we also need to strengthen our partners economically. the eu is the model for economic development but also provides the opportunities for neighbouring countries to broaden their markets. therefore, we have to be open to closer economic integration with our neighbourhood partners. the eu is a successful project of regional integration and as such should be at the forefront of supporting regional cooperation. we have a great deal of experience which can help our neighbours to work and come closer together. i support strengthening the platforms for such cooperation like the eastern partnership and the union for the mediterranean, but also cooperation at the lower level of local and regional authorities. as the saying goes, we do not choose our neighbours but we can choose the relations we build with them, so let us do just that.
rapporteur.– mr president, first of all, i would like to thank all of the nine colleagues who stayed this long and contributed to the discussion. i did not mention it in the beginning, but i would also like to say that it was a very nice project to be rapporteur for this report, and to work with the shadow rapporteurs who came from different political groups but were a team guided by the principle that everybody wanted to contribute positively in order to achieve results in the future, because everybody agrees that the european neighbourhood policy is a very important part of eu external policy. it was really a very interesting cooperation. i would like to offer my thanks and appreciation to commissioner hahn for the many discussions which we had with the representatives of the commission and for his consultation paper, which really focused on the most important issues of the european neighbourhood policy. i think this was a very interesting and good debate; there were many views expressed in it. thank you for your appreciation of my work. some of the criticism was levelled especially at the fact that there are not many results which the enp has achieved since its inception in 2004. i can agree with that, but we learned our lessons, and that is why this report is very timely. it contains many issues and principles which could be used in order not to repeat the mistakes which we committed and to be more prepared for the fast-developing situation in the neighbourhood countries. there was only one statement from which i have to distance myself fully. it was the one which portrayed the eu as the military threat to its neighbours and the institution which causes all bad things in the neighbourhood. nothing is more divorced from life, and i think this i have to reject very adamantly. i think this debate also showed that we are all interested in having an efficient, pragmatic european neighbourhood policy which would serve all the eu countries’ interests and also the interests of our neighbours. so let us hope that this will be the final achievement of this report and of the directive which is being prepared by commissioner hahn for this autumn.

in writing. during this plenary session, we commemorate the 20th anniversary of the srebrenica genocide. in july 1995, 8,372 men and boys were killed in the massacre in the muslim enclave of srebrenica. this massacre is considered the worst in europe since the end of world war ii. the european parliament's committee on women's rights has called for the eu to take action to combat violence against women and girls. it was an honor to meet her and the other survivors. during the interview, saliha osmanovic told me that despite the huge tragedy, she does not feel hatred in herself. and most of all, she made it my heartfelt wish that we never forget what happened in srebrenica 20 years ago, and that we pass this memory on to future generations so that nothing like this ever happens again.

in writing. ‒ eu member states are moving closer to a huge agreement with the us on a transatlantic trade and investment partnership to boost trade in goods and services between them. however, negotiations cannot focus solely on improving economic indicators and trade statistics. we must uphold the eu's high standards for the environment, health and food safety, which are now a model for the whole world, even at the cost of not accepting the agreement. i strongly oppose any reduction in the high standards of consumer and worker protection or in social standards, and i also oppose any limitation of the regulatory powers of the member states. in the name of trade cooperation, the protection of the health of citizens in key areas cannot be denied. in my view, therefore, the agreement should not cover certain areas of public health, such as public health services, genetically modified food, the use of hormones in cattle breeding. in conclusion, i would like to express my regret that the recommendation for negotiations for the european commission is only non-binding and that the european parliament has no formal powers to enter into or bindingly influence trade negotiations. however, at the end of the negotiation process, we will only have to give our opinion on the final form of the agreement by a flat-rate agreement or rejection.
in writing. - mr president with the world around us making a series of agreements on common markets, with russia working with china, china with india and indochina, and with the south american, pacific and united states free trade agreements soon to be concluded, the european union simply cannot pretend that it does not need to expand its markets. these are two equivalent economic systems, with mostly balanced trade indicators, which would only increase if the legislation of the two great powers were gradually harmonized with each other, thus avoiding unnecessary licensing, customs and administrative obstacles. in practice, this would mean more supply and better prices for consumers and traders, and, while it is true that it would bring increased competition, it would also double the internal market. we now have the opportunity to create the strongest bilateral economic bloc that can define international norms.

in writing. ‒ the european union must legislate to ensure the same minimum basis of rights and obligations for all employees. pursuant to article 153 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), it is for the european parliament and the council to adopt, by means of directives, minimum requirements aimed at improving working conditions, protecting workers at the end of their working lives, informing and consulting workers and creating a working environment which protects the health and safety of workers. however, this must not impose disproportionate costs on employers, which hamper the development of smes and could therefore also have a negative impact on employment in this sector. this directive will help to improve the working conditions of seafarers in all eu member states and will contribute to their equal treatment and to the elimination of discrimination in their employment by employers in the member states.

in writing. ‒ the the current military conflicts in syria, iraq, yemen and libya are destabilising the middle east region, damaging the political and economic development of the region, disrupting demographic cohesion and also causing a humanitarian, economic and social crisis for the people of those states. the problems of the middle east have also become the problems of the eu as a whole. thousands of refugees are migrating to the eu, and we are not coping. the stability and security of the middle east region is also threatened on a daily basis by terrorist organisations and supporters of the islamic state. the eu must therefore urgently engage with the un and other major powers to fight terrorist organisations and the islamic state, to stabilise the situation in syria, iraq, yemen and libya as soon as possible, and to prevent the people of these countries from having to leave their homelands in order to save their lives, even at the risk of losing their lives in the mediterranean. the middle east and north africa region is particularly affected by poverty and high inequalities, and only post-conflict economic and social development will bring stability to these regions.
in writing. ‒ i support the revision of the european neighbourhood policy, and in particular the quality report presented by mr kukan. the esp is an important part of the european union's foreign policy and its potential lies in its ability to use a wide range of instruments in the fields of security, diplomacy, economy, trade, development, defence and humanitarian affairs. the esp is also crucial to enhancing the credibility of the european union's foreign policy and our standing on the world stage. the fundamental challenge of the esp must be to bring concrete improvements to the citizens of the partner countries. but it must become more strategic, more focused and more integrated, and it must be politically driven.
in writing. ‒ as the eu is a union of states with common values and interests, the neighbourhood policy must also be a unified expression of the common position of the eu states. naturally, this unified position must be consistent with fundamental values and principles, such as democracy, the rule of law and the protection of human rights. i am convinced that it is the transposition of these principles into concrete actions that will become the stable basis for favourable long-term relations with neighbouring states. however, the current volatile geopolitical situation requires not only continued dialogue and cooperation in finding constructive solutions to current challenges together with our neighbouring countries, but also the introduction of pragmatic security measures to protect eu citizens. i therefore support the strengthening of the eu's external borders and the allocation of the corresponding funds for this purpose.
in writing. ‒ i consider the eu's neighbourhood policy to be an important instrument for ensuring peace and stability. europe today cannot afford to ignore the geopolitical, economic and social changes in its neighbours. it is important to improve cooperation with international organisations and to support financially projects that help alleviate the suffering of people in the world. we also need to set up a control mechanism for these projects. that's why i voted for this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european neighbourhood policy (enp) was created to prevent new dividing lines between the enlarged eu and its neighbours, and we have helped to consolidate the prosperity, stability and security of all the countries involved. on the one hand, i am pleased that the esp is based on the values of democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights, but on the other hand i am sorry that, as a result of the current political and economic changes and under the influence of armed or so-called frozen conflicts, the neighbourhood is undergoing fundamental changes and therefore action is needed. i supported the resolution because i believe it is essential to restructure the neighbourhood policy and to look for ways of changing it in order to build a strong, strategic and lasting partnership that is able to react quickly and flexibly in promoting common interests. at the same time, i feel that the eu must play a more active role in peaceful solutions to existing conflicts that threaten the development of a genuine and effective multilateral dimension of the epc. i expect that, on the basis of the measures taken, the neighbourhood policy will develop into a better adapted and flexible policy framework, able to adapt to the existing diversity of the partner countries.
in writing. ‒ for me and slovakia, ukraine is the most important country in the framework of the neighbourhood policy. its stabilisation and political, economic and financial involvement will have an impact on the prosperity of slovakia, the region and the eu as a whole.
in writing. ‒ the importance of good and strong relations with our neighbours, whether on the eastern side of the union's borders or on the opposite side of the mediterranean, was only realised by many during the recent discussions on migrants, when conflicts in ukraine, syria and libya began to directly affect all member states. the report by mep eduard kukana raises hopes that the planned revision of the eu's neighbourhood policy will ensure more effective cooperation with these countries and offer them a vision of a better future. each country needs to be looked at individually, as the application of a one-size-fits-all neighbourhood policy has not proven successful in the past. i believe that, in addition to the 'more for more' principle, whereby the union strengthens its partnership with those neighbouring countries which are making progress on the path of democratic reform, we should also consider more often the application of the 'less for less' policy towards those who are going in the opposite direction.
in writing. ‒ this report creates a prerequisite for the legal protection of authors and performers in their creative and artistic activities. more than 7 million people are employed in the european union in sectors where intellectual property rights play a significant role. i recognise that commercial activities infringing copyright constitute a threat to the functioning of the digital single market, for example. however, i do not agree with restricting the rights of citizens to present private audiovisual recordings which may feature a building or other historic monument protected by existing copyright legislation.
in writing. the news caused a storm of emotion in slovakia and the czech republic. naturally, citizens are concerned that incorporating this report into the directive, especially not the precise article 46, will prevent them from taking photographs of monuments in the normal way, without even knowing that they are covered by copyright. freedom of panorama is more liberal in our countries, and therefore it is naturally seen as a step backwards. i respect the right of authors to protect their copyright, but in this case, it is also necessary to protect the general public, who have no interest in the commercial exploitation of such images. it is therefore necessary to clarify what is meant by the commercial exploitation of the representation of a work, the manner in which the work is generally disclosed as being protected by copyright and who is liable to pay the author for such disclosure, if any. i therefore voted against the restrictive clause which restricted freedom of panorama.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the initial report on copyright, which aims to take the european parliament's position on the direction to be taken by the future copyright reform in the eu. in order to adapt copyright to the new challenges of the digital age, there is a need to modernise copyright rules in order to develop the european cultural and creative sectors. the sector also deserves attention because it employs more than 7 million people and generates about 4,2% of eu gdp, and employment growth has not stopped even during the economic crisis. in my view, the revision of the current directive should maintain the principle of fair remuneration for rightholders. however, i support the affirmation of the principle of territoriality, whereby each member state will determine fair remuneration within its own cultural policy, and also the principle of subsidiarity, which will allow the member state to adopt specific legislation in accordance with its specific local conditions. these principles should concern in particular the controversial area of the so-called freedom of panorama: taking photographs of monuments or works of art and their subsequent publication on social networks. i believe that taking and publishing for private purposes should be free, but commercial exploitation for profit, which concerns companies, should be clearly and fairly regulated so that copyright is taken into account.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. copyright must adapt to the possibilities of the digital age. on the other hand, european culture must be protected and promoted, which necessarily means protecting the rights of authors. the copyright reform to be introduced must strike a balance between the interests of creators, rights holders and, above all, consumers themselves.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the report assessing the implementation of directive 2001/29/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2001 on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society. copyright as defined in this 2001 european legislation is not perfect. since 2001, the cultural and creative industries have made great progress, contributing significantly to the eu economy, employing over 7 million people and accounting for over 4.2% of eu gdp, according to the latest estimates. the digital market is undergoing major technological advances and it is therefore essential that authors and performers are granted legal protection for their creative and artistic activities, with corresponding remuneration for authors and performers in the digital environment to the same extent as in the analogue environment. the current differences in legislation between member states also create legal uncertainty, which is an obstacle to the creation of a digital single market and to the cross-border availability of copyright-protected content. the commission should therefore adopt a new copyright directive as a matter of urgency to address the current problems.
in writing. ‒ the the digital revolution has also brought many changes in intellectual property law. finding a balance between the rights and obligations of authors and users is increasingly difficult, but necessary. the limitation of copyright, such as a limited period of protection or the freedom of the public to capture a panorama, has its social, cultural and economic justification. the passionate debate on the freedom of panorama, which also allows the reproduction of works placed in the public domain without the author's consent under our copyright law, has shown that member states should continue to decide on the introduction of certain exceptions. the balance between authors' rights and the public has its social, cultural and economic justification, since copyright is intended to protect authors while also serving society.

for the ppe group. common european procedures and practices are always the most effective way of combating unfair practices. the adoption of this regulation on mutual assistance between the administrative authorities of the member states and the european commission is intended to contribute to the proper application of the rules on customs and agricultural matters. the main objective of the regulation is to improve the detection and investigation of customs fraud and thus to combat customs fraud effectively at the level of the european union as a whole. more emphasis should also be placed on preventing and intensifying the exchange of information and available evidence between individual member states. it is important to improve the availability of import, export and transit data as well as data on container movements at national level. as customs officials currently have no possibility to verify whether the declared origin of the goods corresponds to the route of the container, increased cooperation between the administrative authorities of the member states would reduce the abuse of the transit system and allow for a better exchange of information that could serve as evidence in criminal and administrative proceedings in the member states. this regulation also avoids delays and unnecessary loss of time at the investigation stage. it will also ensure that legislation is aligned with the treaty of lisbon as regards the protection of personal data, in particular in the area of procedures and deadlines. i firmly believe that the adoption of this regulation will bring about deeper cooperation between the administrative authorities in the field of customs and thus reduce the number of customs fraud throughout the european union.
