answer the question posed by raising the blue card. as i said at the beginning, i think that common european procedures will best help us to combat fraud, but we have rules, especially on fiscal union, which we need to follow. as far as fiscal union is concerned, i do not think we need new rules, but rather strict compliance with the existing ones.
in writing. fraud related to false declarations increased in 2011 to an annual loss of eur 100 million. member states reported 1 905 cases of fraud and other irregularities linked to incorrect description of goods, representing a loss of eur 107.7 million. this amount relates only to the loss identified by the member states and the commission. as information on some 30 000 suspected cases of fraud is not available, the real scale of the problem is considerably larger. this system was in urgent need of reform as it emerged that the introduction of electronic customs in 2011, where the import and export supporting documents are no longer kept by customs administrations but by economic operators, led to delays in the investigations conducted by the european anti-fraud office in the customs field, as olaf needs the intermediary assistance of customs administrations to obtain these documents. moreover, the three-year limitation period applied to customs documents held by the administration represented additional obstacles to the successful conduct of the investigations. although consumer protection is at a very high level in the european union, it is very important that it is constantly improved and made more effective. it is the duty of the union to combat fraud in the customs field.
in writing. ‒ european union policies must promote and defend human rights and decent work and effectively combat trafficking in human beings. the main objective of the 2014 protocol of the international labour organisation is to eliminate new forms of exploitation and trafficking in slaves. it is estimated that up to 800 000 people in the european union are exposed to new forms of forced labour. since 1930, there have been many changes in the context and form of forced or compulsory labour and it is therefore important that the european union responds adequately to this problem. the protocol should strengthen labour inspection services and more effective enforcement of labour law, as the posting of workers directive allows companies to de facto break the rules and circumvent existing labour law procedures. the protocol also calls on member state governments to take fundamental measures to better protect workers during the difficult recruitment process.
in writing. ‒ the forced labor today takes many forms, often hidden. it affects the most vulnerable groups of the population, especially women and children, but also the long-term unemployed who are unable to find suitable work. such persons accept jobs that they would never have taken otherwise under properly functioning conditions and with sufficient knowledge. forced labour goes hand in hand with lack of education, lack of information and knowledge. it is no longer just prostitution, hard labor in substandard conditions, begging, or other degrading work. in the countries of former eastern europe, a form of forced labor is also seen in various loans and advances from private companies, which people take on the expectation that they will often buy things they do not really need. unfavorable contracts, along with their complicated terms and interest burden, make them modern-day debt slaves who cannot pay back their debts for decades. the european strategy against poverty also needs to coordinate and guide the governments of the eu member states in taking measures to eradicate forced labour from the european area. we can only build a democratic europe if we can guarantee its citizens a decent life and work.
in writing. ‒ in the case of the recommendation concerning the international labour organisation convention on forced or compulsory labour, i voted in favour of this resolution because i am in favour of combating forced labour. in the 21st century, 21 million people are still in forced labor. the 2014 ilo protocol to the 1930 forced or compulsory labour convention updates that convention, providing new tools to combat forced labour and establishing its legally binding nature.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the ilo convention on forced or compulsory labour. labour rights are one of the main pillars of decent work and constitute the main tool to combat labour exploitation. although labour law is very high in the eu, we still encounter forced or compulsory labour. therefore, it is necessary to really think about the risk factors that lead people to forced labour and which the ilo has defined in its latest report on forced labour, such as declining incomes and poverty, vulnerability due to lack of education, illiteracy, vulnerability of specific population groups such as women, children... therefore, member states must take measures to better protect workers, in particular migrant workers, from abuses and fraudulent practices during recruitment. eu policies must defend and promote human rights and decent work, and eliminate trafficking in human beings, whether within or outside the eu.

in writing. ‒ in 2009, the european parliament adopted regulation (ec) no 1007/2009 which banned trade in seal products in the european union. however, the regulation in question has been challenged within the world trade organisation by canada and norway. the commission has therefore decided to extend the period of validity of the general ban on seal products to the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2015. the european commission subsequently decided on a 16-month deadline to prepare the necessary legislation and bring existing legislation into line with world trade organisation decisions and recommendations.
in writing. ‒ the the legislative proposal proposed amends, in line with wto recommendations, the existing exemptions for the hunting of seals and trade in seal products for indigenous peoples for whom hunting is a traditional livelihood and part of their cultural heritage. hunting must be traditionally conducted by inuit or other indigenous communities, must contribute to the livelihood of the community, must not be conducted primarily for commercial purposes and must be conducted in a manner that minimises pain, distress, fear or other forms of suffering to the animals hunted. the need to raise awareness in eu countries about the origin of seal products and their legality is underlined.
in writing. ‒ seal hunting is an integral part of the culture and identity of inuit and other indigenous communities and contributes significantly to their livelihoods, providing food and income to support the life and sustainable livelihoods of the community, preserving and enabling the continuation of the traditional existence of the community and the cultural heritage of the exchange trade. it was therefore necessary to add a derogation for this case in order to allow the placing on the market of seal products under clearly defined conditions. i voted for this resolution.

belarus is one of the last islands of authoritarianism in europe. it is very, very unlikely that this situation will change any time soon. president lukashenko's position in the country is very strong, decisive, almost all-powerful. however, we should be equally open to goodwill gestures that encourage belarus to open up more. the events of the last few months, namely the release of some political prisoners, are one of the main indicators of gradual changes. the signals coming from this country in the last few weeks should be read with the utmost care. but we should definitely take note of them and welcome them as a step in the right direction. these first gestures should not therefore go unanswered by the european union. we should look at and realistically assess the possibilities of lifting some of the restrictive measures that have been applied against belarus in recent years. and this should be done before the presidential elections to be held in belarus in october this year. ladies and gentlemen, i would also like to mention that i am also the rapporteur for the european neighbourhood policy. i would like to see the gradual liberalisation of the regime in belarus translated into its full participation in the european neighbourhood policy. belarus is undeniably a european country, it is really time to see belarus with european, democratic values. (the president agreed to answer the question by raising the blue card (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure). )
blue-card answer.– definitely, yes, we should strengthen civil society in belarus. but we should be fully aware of the complexity and sensitivity of the situation, and we should strengthen the real civil society, not lukashenko’s regime. i am emphasising this because it is not so easy, and we should really have a strategy based on a deep analysis of the real situation in the country.
yes, human trafficking is a gross violation of fundamental rights and a serious form of organized crime. but we should pay particular attention to its new forms. surrogacy is one of them. first, it was women's eggs that were traded, now women are offering their wombs directly. these are mainly women from third countries and socially disadvantaged women. it is necessary to point out this modern form of abuse and slavery under the guise of the so-called rights of the child. surrogacy has become big business, and it needs to be said no. and the trade in the organs of aborted children is absolutely unacceptable. the recently revealed scandalous practices of the international planned parenthood organization must be properly investigated. until then, i demand the suspension of all financial support to this federation from our side. the european union, as the guardian of values and the protector of human rights, cannot turn a blind eye to such a crime. in a developed and civilized europe, there is no place for violations of fundamental human rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the deutsch report on cohesion policy. the sixth cohesion report assesses the situation in the field of cohesion policy and provides guidance on the future management and possible development of cohesion policy. the eu's cohesion policy is of particular importance for our region, as it plays a major role in reducing disparities between regions. it affects small and medium-sized enterprises, innovation, education, many areas of life. the report also rightly points out the shortcomings that need to be addressed in the area of payment difficulties and the need to address the future assessment of cohesion in cross-border european regions. the long-term thrust of the report is to plan for the period after 2020 with citizens and cooperating communities at the heart of cohesion policy.
in writing ‒ the channelling of eu resources to co-finance projects during the financial crisis helped to uncover shortfalls in member states' public finances, which had a positive impact on job creation. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. despite the cohesion policy, which has mitigated the impact of the economic and financial crisis, the reduction of regional disparities has not been achieved, as is evident in the poorest regions of the union. local and regional actors have to bear the burden of late payments from union funds, most notably the impact of the €24.8 billion of outstanding payments at the end of 2014 in the european social fund, the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund programmes. the commission must therefore take measures to mitigate the negative effects, while taking into account local problems and specificities in the granting of aid. the review of the measures taken is also an opportunity to reassess the eu's priorities and their impact on budgetary management.
in writing. ‒ the cohesion policy investments provide long-term stability to regions by securing the flow of funds even during the sharp decline in national public and private investment that accompanied the financial crisis. i am therefore very concerned about the significant delay in the implementation of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020 and the non-use of the appropriations already earmarked for 2014 for the european structural and investment funds. such unpreparedness and complications mean that we need to continue to simplify procedures at both eu and member state level and reduce red tape in order to increase the availability and better use of the euro funds. in this context, i would stress that public procurement is a tool of good governance and should be legislated in such a way as to allow for the swift and flexible use of the european funds.
in writing ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution on investing in jobs and growth by promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion in the union. cohesion policy is an important tool for achieving the objectives of horizon 2020. the report presented adequately assessed the positive impact of the policy, but also identified the areas of concern and the objectives for its future direction.
in writing ‒ although the sixth cohesion report was submitted late, i voted in favour of the report because it not only gives an overview of the developments to date, but also looks ahead and points to the main objectives of investment in cohesion policy in the period 2014-2020. in the report, i particularly welcome the fact that cohesion policy investments have provided stability to regions by securing the flow of funds in a situation where national public and private investments have declined or even stopped altogether. on the contrary, i find it very worrying that the disparities between regions continue to widen and that many jobs created since 2000 are being lost. i consider very positive the measures aimed at supporting smes and improving the employment situation of young people. however, i am convinced that if we really want to help smes, we must create conditions for them that not only simplify procedures and eliminate unnecessary red tape, but also help them, above all, to draw on funds.
‒ i did not support the report because i fundamentally disagree with the way it views cohesion policy. cohesion policy, according to the report, has prevented the collapse of public investment in the eu as a result of member states' austerity measures and has also helped to reduce unemployment. however, this view sees cohesion policy funds as 'free money', which is not the case. all the money in cohesion policy comes from the budgets of the member states and ultimately from taxes on employees and entrepreneurs. cohesion policy has therefore not generated any new investment or employment growth, but has only replaced some of the more efficient and genuinely required investments and jobs in the private sector with less efficient investments and jobs for which there was no real demand in the market.
the european year of solidarity between generations has highlighted the importance of older people in an ageing european society. in this context, the report of mr kukana also drew attention to the situation of mothers whose pensions are negatively affected by maternity and unpaid care for children and family members. i have always stressed the need to tackle this problem with concrete measures. it is neither fair nor right that our society punishes mothers financially, when its prosperity directly depends on new generations of citizens bringing these mothers into the world and educating them in responsibility and solidarity with others. i supported this report and i hope that concrete proposals will soon be on the table. i also appreciate that the european parliament has accepted my proposal in time to extend the year of active ageing to a year of solidarity between generations.
in writing. ‒ 2012 was the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations in the eu, which saw the launch of a number of initiatives at eu level to improve quality of life for older people and to respond to the new challenges posed by demographic change. the phenomenon affects almost every eu member state and is a social, political and economic issue that requires increasing attention. the parliament's report assesses the year's achievements and, among other things, states that the initiatives started should be continued. the report highlights the importance of convening the upcoming european union convention on demographic change, which could add new dimensions to the challenges posed by the phenomenon. it also encourages member states to use the available eu funding opportunities to achieve policy objectives on active ageing: the european structural and investment funds, horizon 2020, the european programme for employment and social innovation, the public health programme. the central european region also needs eu resources in this area to meet the changing health, education and economic needs of older generations. in accordance with the above, i voted in favour of the report by mr eduard kukan.
in writing ‒ the ageing of the population is a fact that the european union must face up to. the year 2012 brought a number of activities coordinated by the union which demonstrated the possibility of active ageing and ways of involving older people in different activities. co-paternity and solidarity with the older generation will contribute to improving the quality of life of these people and cannot be limited to the allocation of funds. the experiences and knowledge of an older generation can be motivating and inspiring for the succeeding generations and can contribute to economic development and growth.
‒ i take a very positive view of the issue of ageing and population ageing, mainly because i recognise the value of what older people have and can still offer to society. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the rapporteur for the report he has produced and to commend the progress made in the framework of the 2012 european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations. i was happy to support the resolution, but i am sure we can all agree that there is still room for improvement in this population. i consider this to be important, particularly because this target group is the largest but also the most vulnerable group of the european population and their problems and needs are still not being addressed sufficiently at member state level. however, i believe that, as in 2012, we will continue to actively address the problems and needs of older people, thereby contributing not only to improving and enhancing their lives, but also to creating conditions for a better and more qualitative ageing of the younger generation of today.
‒ i did not support the report because it calls on the member states and the commission to take measures that will lead to an increase in the financial and regulatory burden.
‒ the report builds on the results achieved in the framework of 2012, which was declared the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. this year's objective was to create a culture of active ageing in europe and many of its objectives have been met and reflected positively to such an extent that the report calls for the concept of active ageing to be continued, in particular in promoting longer working lives for people who want and can work into old age, as well as the principle of non-discrimination on grounds of age and good access to healthcare. i supported the report because the problem of the ageing population of the european union is a reality that will become increasingly important in the future, and the concept of active ageing will concern us all in the future, and therefore we need to think about how it can be supported and developed.
in writing. ‒ the commission's 2011 white paper on transport states that mobility and employment must be increased at eu level, by reducing europe's dependence on oil imports and by reducing transport's carbon dioxide emissions by 60% by 2050. the parliament supports the objectives, but points out that there is a significant gap between the objectives and the means needed to achieve and finance them. parliament says that we must move towards stronger and more competitive, but also more environmentally friendly, transport as part of our political objectives. the text states that the implementation of trans-european transport networks is also a prerequisite for balancing transport modes and closing infrastructure gaps, and that this may be of particular importance in closing the gaps in central europe. transport policy developments should take greater account of the mobility needs and safety of eu citizens. this should be reflected in the construction of safer roads, the modernisation of urban mobility and infrastructure design, the development of intelligent vehicles and the focus on pedestrians, cyclists and vulnerable road users. i voted for the ideas.
‒ the 2011 white paper on transport sets ambitious transport targets for the eu, which should be met by 2050 at the latest. trends in the world economy require the building of a strong, competitive and safe system in all transport sectors, which takes into account the need to improve the quality of the environment and reduce the need for energy efficiency. the transport sector is also an important source of employment growth. the achievement of the objectives of the white paper and the creation of a fully integrated single european transport area requires the monitoring and reassessment of the performance of the individual tasks in the light of the ultimate objective and current developments in world transport.
‒ i consider transport and the creation of a single transport area to be very important also for economic growth, job growth and the quality of services in transport, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution on the implementation of the white paper on transport.
‒ europe needs a competitive transport system to increase mobility and promote growth and jobs. the commission proposal also aims to reduce europe's dependence on oil imports and to reduce carbon emissions from transport by 60% by 2050. i support the effective implementation of the white paper on transport because i believe that transport needs to become more efficient, cleaner, safer and more reliable.
‒ i did not support the report because i do not agree with many of the measures it proposes to support the development of eu transport and infrastructure. the report places too much emphasis on improving social conditions, reducing dependence on fossil fuels and other measures that will increase the regulatory burden and ultimately harm the very passengers they are supposed to protect.
in writing ‒ i fully support all measures that will lead to the advancement of women's scientific and university careers. in this area, all obstacles, unequal treatment and any discrimination, including prejudices, which are both a brake and a gross violation of fundamental human rights, must be removed. at the same time, conditions must be created to reconcile working life and the development of women's knowledge with regard to their maternal role.
‒ it is important that we promote the skilled employment of women in the labour market. however, i firmly believe that the introduction of quotas to determine the number of women in senior positions in the university and scientific sphere is certainly not the right solution to this support. that is why i voted against the ep resolution on women's scientific and university careers.
in writing ‒ despite the increasing number of female university students in europe, we continue to see women underrepresented in science and technology. this is evidenced by the statistics which show that in europe women currently represent only 33% of researchers, 20% of university professors and only 15.5% of heads of higher education institutions. i am personally very pleased that the issue of women in science and higher education is also beginning to receive greater attention within the eu. i am convinced that women represent a highly educated and intellectual potential for the field in question, which is proving to be very underutilized. on the other hand, i am pleased that flexible organisations are already increasingly accepting women in their key positions, not only for reasons of social justice, but also for their real skills and attitudes. although women are increasingly taking up occupations that were until recently the domain of men, i too continue to find that some still consider the connection between women and careers to be unnatural. i welcome all the actions and measures that address the elimination of stereotypes and prejudices against women and address the under-representation of women in science, technology, engineering and higher education.
in writing - i did not support the proposal. i do not agree with the measures presented, many of which increase the regulatory burden, ultimately in many cases harm women more than they help, are examples of positive discrimination or interfere with the powers of the member states. these are things like quotas for women on company boards, a call to teach children about 'equality' in schools, a direct call to support women in certain professions and so on.
‒ the report addresses the barriers faced by women in professions at all levels. it focuses on the fields of science, technology, but also on academic careers and management positions, where women are least represented. women who want to pursue their careers after having a family should be able to do so. more day care and nursery schools, adaptation of working conditions, such as more flexible working hours, the possibility of dividing parental leave and taking it up to the child's 12th birthday. these are just a few of the many tools that would make it possible for women to avoid having to choose between career and family.
i voted against this report because every family has the right to live freely according to their faith and to choose educational programs for their children without being discriminated against. parents are their children's first and foremost teachers. this right is recognised by the universal declaration of human rights, the convention on the rights of the child and the european treaties. the use of the term 'gender', which is not legally defined and whose meaning varies according to the context, leaves room for different interpretations and is not appropriate to refer to discrimination between women and men as it is also spoken of in the european treaties. the gender identities referred to in the report are not based on contracts or reality and are an ideological social construct with no place in compulsory education for children. this is just another report of reports that violate the sovereignty of the member states.
in writing ‒ i have no doubt about the importance of educating citizens in the eu. certainly, the education of girls in particular requires special attention. the lack of education often results in a lower social and societal status. however, the report submitted falls within the exclusive competence of the member states. it also addresses issues of sex education and training for children in schools, the inclusion of lgbti issues in the curriculum and other sensitive issues that member states have to address in light of their conditions, development, culture and history. this requires mutual tolerance, respect and understanding between eu countries.
‒ the rapporteur's own-initiative report on empowering girls in the eu through education goes beyond the clearly defined competences of the eu and into areas that belong only to the member states. in addition to the commendable efforts to ensure girls' access to girls, it demands and calls on eu member states to recognise mandatory gender-sensitive sexuality education and so-called sexual and reproductive rights as fundamental human rights of self-determination, including the controversial right to abortion. the commission also called on the member states to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet in a safe and secure manner. i firmly reject the report and such european attempts to encroach on the rights of the member states and to interfere in the private and family affairs of their citizens.
in writing. - it is well known that the greatest enemies of the blood-thirsty system are educated girls. and that's why, unfortunately, they're not afraid to take any measure to prevent girls from getting their hands on books. fortunately, girls born in the union don't have to worry about things like what happened to malala. of course, they can go to school and, in theory, have every chance of benefiting from the education system and, therefore, from the labour market, in accordance with their abilities. theoretically speaking. in practice, however, the numbers are skewed. gender equality in society can only be achieved through reform of the education system. this is the primary ground for overcoming stereotypes. the goal should be clear to all of us. that's why i find it outrageous that controversial issues of conscience and ethics are being brought up again. this is not a forum where we have to deal with the beliefs or personal lives of teachers. nor is it where we have to fight the symbolic battles of separation of church and state. it's time for our education to be about real equality, about ending poverty, about ending violence against women.
in writing ‒ in the european institutions, we increasingly encounter repeated attempts to overstep their competence and to disrespect the sovereignty of the member states, as well as the infringement of the inalienable rights of parents to bring up their children. i'm against the growing pressure to push gender ideology. the proposals for its introduction are aimed at indoctrinating society and, in particular, in the rodrigues report, at indoctrinating the very youngest, our children. i cannot agree with that, which is why i voted against this resolution.
in writing ‒ education and training for girls and women is an important european value, a fundamental human right and a basis for the empowerment of women and girls at social, cultural and professional levels. worldwide, 17 percent of the adult population is illiterate, and two thirds of them are women. education is a tool that enables women to gain economic independence. therefore, measures aimed at implementing gender equality at all levels of the education system must be effective and verifiable. member states must also integrate childcare and early childhood education into their education systems to enable parents to find a balance between work and family life. member states must ensure equal access to education for girls and boys regardless of age, gender, socioeconomic status, cultural background or religion. the principle of equality between women and men should be addressed in curricula at all stages of education.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report because it fundamentally interferes with the competences of the member states in the field of education, as in other areas.
in writing. ‒ while the ecr group is a strong supporter of progress in equality of both girls and boys in the area of education, the report goes far beyond the remit and responsibilities of the committee on women’s rights and gender equality (femm) and of parliament, particularly in the area of education. the main areas of concern for the ecr deal with the prescriptive nature of the ‘training and curriculum’ section of the report, namely the suggested promotion of gender equality in member states’ comprehensive sex and relationship education programmes, the consideration of making sex and relationship education compulsory in the school curricula for all primary and secondary school children and the insistence on gender equality as a criterion for production of educational materials and gender-aware tutoring. some of the recommendations in the report constitute intrusion into the citizen’s beliefs, such as the need to include strategies for reflection on teachers’ own identity, beliefs, values, prejudices, expectations, attitudes and gender representations, as well as on their teaching practices, in teachers training. considering that neither the femm committee, nor parliament were given a mandate in the area of education and the fact that the above cited concerns constitute a very significant part of the report, the ecr was unable to support it.
in writing. ‒ in its report on the eea and switzerland, the parliament sent an important signal to the efta states by expressing its concern about the delay in transposing legislation affecting the single market. the ep stresses that the substantive legislation on the single market is implemented in time and with the least possible delay by the efta states belonging to the eea. the report calls, inter alia, for the removal of obstacles to cross-border labour mobility in order to achieve a more complete internal market, in the interests of eu citizens who want to benefit from mobility. it also agrees with the eu's rejection in july 2014 of the request of the swiss authorities to renegotiate the agreement on the free movement of persons. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ i appreciate the strong and long-standing relations between the eu and switzerland, as well as the efta countries that are members of the eea. the eea agreement is a key driver and has contributed to increased peace, prosperity and growth in europe. the european union should continue to strive to expand the single market, create a level playing field, create new jobs and promote entrepreneurship, including through support for small and medium-sized enterprises. in order to promote the development of eu relations with eea countries, i supported this report.
in writing ‒ i abstained from the vote on the report. i agree with many of her observations, but i disagree with her view of restricting immigration to switzerland based on the valid referendum result. the report points out how reciprocity between the eea and switzerland is essential and how restricting migration can create imbalances and jeopardise the benefits of the agreements for eu member states. the restriction of immigration in switzerland is of course unfortunate, but since it is a democratic decision of the citizens, it must be respected absolutely. furthermore, all cross-border trade is mutually beneficial and therefore there is no need to talk about any limitation of reciprocity or of the benefits of cross-border trade.
‒ regional instability and conflict and the rise of isis in neighbouring conflict areas are affecting the mass influx of migrants and flows of displaced persons, and thus the number of individual attempts to enter the european union. the european union and the member states must find an effective solution and strengthen existing cooperation in order to prevent further loss of life, prevent further disembarkations of smuggling vessels, speed up and streamline the processing of asylum applications in the member states, return immediately those who do not meet the criteria and fully integrate those who have been granted asylum. the european union must apply a zero-tolerance policy on trafficking in human beings and put pressure on member states to work closely with europol, frontex, easo and eurojust to combat these criminal networks of traffickers by identifying how and where they operate and preventing their departure.
in writing. ‒ i voted for aid to war refugees because we have to deal with this crisis and the european union has to deal with it. it creates an incentive for member states to do much more on all three pillars of the problem, especially prevention, that is, foreign aid, military if necessary, humanitarian aid for countries that are now hosting millions of refugees who are bearing a 100-fold burden. the common protection of the external borders should also be strengthened, and i expect further relaxation of the conditions under which the selected countries attract not only refugees but also illegal migrants, and that the separation of refugees from economic migrants finally begins in good time. the fact that one part of the resolution refers to uncertified mandatory quotas does not mean that we prefer to leave things as they are. this would mean the closure of the schengen borders and possibly the disintegration of the union as a whole. how much we've already sacrificed over the last 10 years to get into that european union.
in writing. ‒ the problem of migration and refugees cannot leave anyone indifferent to the stories of people fleeing the threat of war and violence to save their lives. we have already adopted several important resolutions on this subject in the european parliament, but the problems of migrants and refugees have deepened. a year ago we called on the commission, the council and the relevant security services to take measures to break up the smuggling gangs and groups and to prevent people from dying in the mediterranean. a year later, we find that smuggling networks have spread inland and people are no longer dying at sea but also inland, using the balkan route. i support all the points in the resolution, but i cannot agree with the point which establishes a permanent, binding system for the distribution of asylum seekers between the 28 member states, using a mandatory distribution key, the so-called quotas, which is why i did not vote in favour of the motion for a resolution. because i can't see how we're going to redistribute migrants to countries they don't want to go to. will we redistribute them by force? i can't relate to that. they left their own before the violence, and we're supposed to use violence again?
in writing ‒ i did not support the proposal because i reject the quotas for the mandatory redistribution of migrants between eu member states. this proposal promotes the breach of the existing rules on border protection and, moreover, does not solve the whole situation, but only leads to the creation of further new problems.
in writing ‒ i did not support the joint motion for a resolution because i reject the introduction of a permanent, binding system for the distribution of asylum seekers. it is not possible to pay for the holes in the common european asylum policy hastily by making the crisis mechanism permanent. when a window breaks, duct tape is a stopgap, not a solution. one-off assistance to greece, italy and hungary is essential to ensure that the registration of asylum seekers does not fail. but we know that the solution to the migration crisis must also include better protection of the external borders, a speedy asylum procedure and, with it, the effective deportation of unsuccessful asylum seekers from the eu.
in writing ‒ the parts of the resolution that offer quotas as a solution, i couldn't support. solidarity and help cannot be forced. however, i agree with many of the calls in the text, which is why i abstained in the final vote. it is important to set up the so-called hotspots as soon as possible and to ensure their efficient functioning. i also support the updating of safe countries of origin, which will allow for faster processing of asylum applications and direct our aid to those who really need it.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the eu approach that a comprehensive regional solution is a prerequisite for peace in the middle east. we are also concerned about peace in the region, as the union is israel's largest trading partner and the palestinians' largest donor of aid. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. parliament condemns the continuing expansion of israeli settlements. the report also calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. i supported the report.
in writing the long-running conflict between israel and the arab states, particularly palestine, not only affects the economies of these countries but also affects the economic and financial interests of the european union. attempts at lasting peace have met with only partial and short-lived success. the situation is also aggravated by political instability in neighbouring countries, particularly in syria. the eu is one of israel's largest trading partners and is also the largest aid provider to palestine. it is precisely this position that the eu must make more intensive and targeted use of in the process of peaceful settlement of the middle east problems. at the same time, i consider it essential to use all control mechanisms to ensure that trade and aid are used in a transparent manner and do not contribute to the possible support of terrorist groups and further escalation of tensions in this area.
in writing. - it would be nice to see some results in this peace process. somehow, it feels like we've been going around and around the same problem for decades, and we're not a hair's breadth closer to a solution. and yet generations are growing up on one side in fear of the radicalism of the other side, and on the other side in despair, isolated, in abject poverty, in refugee camps without education and without hope. recently, the eu finally took a stand and committed itself to palestinian statehood, while recognising israel's legitimate concerns for its own security. i think this is the way. at the same time, as mediators, we must facilitate dialogue between the parties. we need to create opportunities where israeli and palestinian youth, thinkers, teachers, scientists can exchange ideas, get to know each other without political pressure. let us not forget that syria and lebanon can play a key role in the peace process.
in writing. ‒ achieving peace in the middle east is a key priority for the international community and a necessary prerequisite for stability and security in the region. the eu has repeatedly reaffirmed its support for a two-state solution to the israeli-palestinian conflict based on the 1967 borders, with jerusalem as the capital of both states. the eu is israel's largest trading partner and the largest provider of aid to palestine, so the eu's role in the middle east peace process must be dominant. however, both the israeli and palestinian sides must refrain from actions that could provoke further escalation of violence, including hate speech and public incitement. this could jeopardise further negotiations and the eu's efforts to bring about a peace process in the middle east.
in writing. ‒ parliament recalls that human rights violations continue to prevail in belarus. progress has been made in some areas, but much remains to be done before a democratic state is established. since 1994, there have been no free, democratic and internationally acceptable elections. the ep also calls on the commission to take action to support the efforts of belarusian civil society, independent media and ngos with financial and political means to support the democratic aspirations of the belarusian people. i supported the report.
in writing ‒ despite progress in cooperation with belarus in some sectoral policies such as higher education, training, digital market, energy, food security and culture, human rights violations in belarus, including intimidation of human rights defenders, police raids against human rights organisations and confiscation of their equipment, and forced evictions from belarus, persist. the european union must ensure that its resources are not used to repress civil society organisations, human rights defenders, free-lance journalists and opposition leaders. the situation of national minorities in the country is critical because the leading representatives of these minorities are often replaced by representatives promoted by state authorities, thus violating one of the fundamental human freedoms, namely freedom of association. the belarusian authorities must ensure that democratic principles, human rights and fundamental freedoms are respected in accordance with the universal declaration of human rights and international and regional human rights instruments ratified by belarus.
in writing despite some progress in some sectoral policies, such as education, training, culture, food, energy, belarus remains among the countries where the rule of law is violated and fundamental human rights and freedoms are not respected. belarus has not yet held free and democratic elections that would help resolve the situation. the state interferes in several spheres, in particular in freedom of the press, speech and association, with undemocratic laws. the commission must use all diplomatic, political and financial means to support civil society in belarus. financial assistance provided by the eu must be controlled to prevent misuse.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the situation in belarus. in the run-up to the forthcoming presidential elections in belarus, the eu has an interest in ensuring that the elections are held in accordance with internationally recognised standards, that the opposition has unrestricted access to all government-controlled means of communication and can participate in the elections on equal terms, and that a transparent counting of votes is ensured. after years of stagnation in eu-belarus cooperation, the first official visit of the ep delegation for relations with belarus took place in minsk on 18 and 19 june 2015. the resolution also welcomes the constructive role played by belarus in facilitating the ceasefire agreement in ukraine. the progress made in sectoral cooperation with belarus in the areas of higher education, training, digital market, energy, food security, culture and others is also positively assessed. on the other hand, we would point out that belarus remains the only country in europe that still carries out the death penalty.
‒ i supported the motion as i agree with its calls for greater respect for human rights and democratic principles.
in writing ‒ the major economic and financial crisis, which has been shrinking europe's regions since 2008, has, among other things, caused a divergence from some of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. however, in addition to the problems of migration, the european union will also have to urgently address the problems of economic and financial sustainability, social prosperity and job creation for young people under 25 in the near future. in addition to these challenges, the european union's leaders must not forget that our continent is ageing permanently, and must also give due attention to the ageing of the population and the depopulation of rural areas. many of these objectives can only be achieved if the social economy is functioning, as social economy enterprises have shown themselves to be more resilient to economic shocks and have stronger links with local and regional structures. social entrepreneurship and social innovation will be essential for the further development of the social economy. it is therefore crucial to pay particular attention to education and training. the european union must instill in young people, from an early age, this necessary enthusiasm for innovation and entrepreneurship.
in writing social entrepreneurship is an important tool for maintaining economic and financial sustainability, promoting sustainable job creation and social development. the priority of social entrepreneurship is to address the broader social problem of the community and the individual. the profits from such enterprises are not used for personal purposes but are invested in social purposes. it increases the durability and value of such a business. in order to allow such a business to develop more widely, it is necessary to create appropriate legislative and economic conditions. the commission, together with the council, must therefore set in motion all the processes necessary to promote and develop such businesses successfully in all eu member states.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the european parliament's report on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment, as the social and solidarity economy currently comprises 2 million social and solidarity economy enterprises, representing 10% of enterprises in the union and providing employment for some 14 million people. i hope that this own-initiative report of the european parliament will lead to an increase in awareness in this area, since, unfortunately, so far very little attention has been paid to the social and solidarity economy at european and member state level. i support social enterprises in particular because they put into practice the principles of solidarity and responsibility and combine the interests of members, users and the general or social interest, which takes precedence over the ruthless pursuit of profit or the accumulation of capital. i therefore join the call to the commission and the member states to create a favourable environment for the creation of business incubators for social and solidarity-based enterprises and to create and effectively promote an online platform for the exchange of data between social investors and social entrepreneurs, the social innovation europe platform.

in writing. ‒ while social entrepreneurship is becoming an increasingly popular tool to tackle unemployment, i continue to find that many people are still afraid to start their own business. in my experience, one of the biggest concerns of new entrepreneurs is that they do not have the necessary skills, do not have enough business education or do not have the right contacts to support their entrepreneurial ambitions. i am pleased that up to 40% of young europeans are interested in starting a small business or self-employment, so i think social entrepreneurship seems to be the right choice for them. i supported this current report because i believe that innovation in social entrepreneurship creates social value and at the same time allows people to be entrepreneurs, even if they have limited financial resources. i also consider it important that social entrepreneurship and social innovation provide an opportunity to respond in an innovative and entrepreneurial way to social needs that are often not met either by the market or by the state. i expect that this report will also make social entrepreneurship a major challenge for all member states which are lagging behind in this area.

in writing ‒ unemployment remains a major problem for the european union. in particular, youth unemployment, which is truly alarming in some member states, as in spain, for example, more than 21% of the population is unemployed. these high figures can be attributed to the economic crisis, but the problem is that according to several studies, there are more than 2 million jobs in europe that are unfilled by employers due to labour market imbalances and lack of labour mobility. there are other problems such as labour market segmentation, the presence of a mismatch between the skills offered and those required in the labour market, together with the growing share of long-term unemployment. reforms are needed to create a competitive labour market, increasing labour market flexibility and career orientation and improving the match between skills and jobs, including greater synergies between education systems and business actors.
in writing the biggest employment problem in the eu is the long-term problem of youth unemployment, which currently stands at an average of 21.4%, despite two million job vacancies. in addition to lack of mobility, this is mainly due to a mismatch between the required and offered job skills and qualifications. education and training are not sufficiently responsive to labour market demand, resulting in high unemployment among young people with unusable skills. changes in this area are relatively slow, and as the labour market is subject to rapid change, the gap in skills demanded and offered may become even wider. the union, in cooperation with the member states, must therefore urgently analyse the labour market situation and adopt flexible measures in the field of education, training and youth to reverse this unfavourable situation.

in writing. - i voted for mrs stevens' report. it is unacceptable that forced labor is still present in modern society and economy. despite a convention dating back to 1930 that has been ratified by almost every country in the world, according to the international labour organization, there are still at least 20.9 million victims of forced labor worldwide. to address the problem more effectively, the ilo has drawn up an additional protocol to the convention. the purpose of the protocol is to address shortcomings in implementation in order to ensure protection and compensation for victims of forced labour. it is a positive step that the protocol requires ilo member states to develop their policies and action plans for the effective and lasting elimination of forced labour. the protocol also emphasises the prevention of forced labour and the compensation and protection of victims, which are also important elements of the problem's eradication. the ratification of the protocol by member states will facilitate action against traffickers. as parts of the protocol fall within the eu's competence, a council decision is required for its ratification. this required the consent of parliament, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ despite many steps taken to end the use of forced labour, there are still more than 20 million people who are forced to perform forced labour. in accordance with the case law of the court of justice of the european union, member states cannot decide to ratify the protocol outside the framework of the institutions of the european union, as parts of the protocol fall within the competence of the european union. the draft council decision empowers member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, those parts of the protocol which fall within the competence of the european union and recommends that they do so, if possible, by the end of 2016. ratification of the protocol would be a major step forward in the fight against trafficking in human beings, labour exploitation and the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ the convention on forced or compulsory labour became binding on slovakia in 1990. by adopting it, all member states committed themselves to combating the use of forced or compulsory labour in all its forms as soon as possible. nevertheless, it is estimated that there are currently 21 million victims of such practices, generating illicit profits of around usd 150 billion and damaging the economic interests of the union. it is therefore necessary to re-evaluate the strengthening of the fight against forced or compulsory labour and adapt it to the conditions of the 21st century. at the 103rd session of the international labour conference in june 2014, a new ilo protocol was adopted, which strengthens international cooperation in combating forced or compulsory labour and introduces new measures, in particular on trafficking in human beings, improving protection for victims and providing access to compensation. states that ratify the ilo convention must develop a national strategy and action plan to combat forced labour. prevention is important in this process, which includes in particular informing vulnerable persons and protecting them against possible fraudulent recruitment practices. the member states are hereby authorised to ratify, in the interest of the eu, those parts of the protocol which fall within the eu's competence.
in writing. ‒ the in the context of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising the member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the 2014 protocol to the ilo convention on forced or compulsory labour, i am keenly aware of the experience of the recent years of recession, when in our country alone almost 15% of people were unemployed for some time. many of them have thus found themselves in financial straits that make them easy prey to the illegal practices of modern slavery, not only abroad but also at home. i therefore welcome the recommendation to ratify the ilo convention on forced or compulsory labour, which will facilitate the fight against such traffickers. moreover, the number of victims of forced or compulsory labor worldwide is still estimated at over 21 million today. i appreciate that the convention introduces an obligation to ensure their identification, release, protection, recovery and rehabilitation, as well as that other provisions require ratifying states to provide all victims with access to compensation and to ensure that competent authorities are empowered not to prosecute them for the illegal activities they were forced to commit.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, forced labour is not a historical concept, but a very real reality today. i therefore consider it extremely important that all eu member states should join the international labour organisation (ilo) convention on this subject as soon as possible. this convention is important to make enforcement and judicial cooperation in the prevention and prosecution of forced labour more effective, to protect workers from exploitation and to provide compensation to victims. the right to work is one of the fundamental human rights and it is crucial that we use all means to ensure that citizens have the right conditions and are protected from becoming victims of tyranny. to do this, the adoption of this convention by the ep is one of the first steps.
in writing. ‒ helping victims of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of forced labour is an essential part of the fight against this crime. i very much welcome the fact that the 2014 additional protocol calls for effective measures to identify, release, protect, recover and rehabilitate these victims, and also focuses on their compensation and protection from prosecution. i agree that member states should be mandated to ratify the protocol to the forced labour convention, 1930, concerning labour exploitation and trafficking in human beings for that purpose. under eu law and its interpretation as established by the case law of the european court of justice, member states could not ratify certain parts of the protocol falling within the eu's competence without an eu mandate, and i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation. however, it should be recalled that any other form of trafficking in human beings, whether sexual exploitation, trafficking in human organs or a new form of so-called surrogacy, must be tackled with equal vigour.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the proposal for a european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision authorising the member states to ratify, in the interest of the eu, the 2014 protocol to the 1930 international labour organisation convention on forced or compulsory labour, as regards articles 1 to 4 of the protocol relating to matters concerning judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the protocol requires member states to develop a national policy and action plan for the effective and systematic suppression of forced labour and to adopt measures to implement the provisions of the protocol. the 2014 protocol addresses fundamental rights, victims and the fight against trafficking in human beings, a crime that has consequences not only for individuals but also for society and the economy as a whole. the ratification of the protocol by the member states will facilitate the fight against trafficking in human beings and therefore the member states should ratify the protocol as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as i support the fight against forced labour and measures to eliminate it.
in writing. ‒ i supported the protocol to the ilo convention on forced labour. in this context, parliament authorised the member states to accept those parts of the protocol which fall within the competence of the european union, since the member states cannot decide to accept them on their own. i fully support the aims of the forced or compulsory labour convention and find it sad that 80 years after its adoption, its main objective, the total elimination of forced labour, has not been fulfilled. i therefore think that this issue needs to be addressed more intensively, in particular by standing up for the victims of forced labour, by helping these victims and their access to justice and adequate compensation.

in writing. ‒ the in the light of this proposal, i call on the council to subject the substance to more stringent control measures. the substance 5- ((2-aminopropyl) indole is a synthetic indole derivative substituted on the phenyl side of the indole ring system. it appears to be a stimulant that may also have hallucinogenic effects. the available information and data suggest that acute toxicity of 5- ((2-aminopropyl) indole may cause adverse effects in humans such as tachycardia and body overheating, and may also cause pupil dilation (mydriasis), agitation and tremor. there are no published studies assessing its acute and chronic toxicity, effects on mental health, behaviour or potential addictiveness, as only limited information and data are available. however, the available evidence and information provides sufficient grounds for subjecting 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole to control measures across the union. due to the health risks it poses, as evidenced by its presence in several reported cases of death, and the fact that it has no medical value or use, 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole should be subject to control measures throughout the union.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation. experience has shown that centrally managed and 'bottom-up' development policies and programmes are not able to provide solutions to the problems of sustainable development and poverty reduction, and aid does not reach those for whom it is intended effectively. not only does the eu not see concrete positive outcomes that have a real impact on the lives of local people, but it also suffers the negative consequences, currently in the form of a migration crisis, as people from developing countries are driven from their homes by the poor situation. i therefore consider it important that part of european budgetary aid be earmarked directly for the financing of local authorities. this is particularly true of countries where there are serious human rights violations. in such cases, the eu may suspend cooperation with central governments and continue to provide assistance through local authorities and civil society organisations.
in writing. ‒ the level of commitment of local authorities to achieving the objectives set is always a key issue in development cooperation. the eu's good intentions to help local communities in their daily democratic struggles or in the fight against poverty are frustrated when most of the funds end up in the pockets of the corrupt or when the other side is indifferent and will not cross two straw. in this respect, local authorities have a key role to play in this matter, and it often only makes sense to start any kind of cooperation if the conditions are right for direct, open communication with local authorities and there is the political will to achieve results. otherwise, even if we work hard, our development aid will be money thrown out the window. i therefore welcome the report which highlights the importance of this issue. the next step for us is to really take a development policy that has concrete results in the light of all this. otherwise, the eu will be seen as a plain cow by corrupt governments in third countries. our own citizens have a legitimate demand to see results for the euros they invest.

in writing. ‒ the european simplified procedure will help consumers and smes in particular to recover their claims. the limit for proceedings in crossborder commercial and civil matters is increased from the current eur 2 000 to eur 10 000 in respect of a legal person and to eur 5 000 in respect of a natural person. postal and electronic delivery shall be equally eligible. by 3 years at the latest from the entry into force of the regulation, member states are obliged to introduce video and teleconferencing, while the right of the parties to be heard in person is preserved. this reduces the costs of the procedure and the length of the procedure. the minimum amount of court fees shall be eur 35, the maximum is set at a ceiling of 5% of the value of the claim. each member state is required to set a minimum income threshold below which the parties will not be required to pay court fees. member states must ensure administrative support and public awareness of this type of procedure.

in writing. ‒ air pollution is not bound by borders, which is why it is important to limit emissions consciously within eu legal frameworks. the new proposal for a directive aims to fill a gap in eu law, as there are currently no specific provisions on emissions from medium combustion plants. emissions from such combustion plants have significant negative effects on health and the environment, not least economically. the parliament's report calls for the new rules not to impose excessive administrative burdens on smes. it is known that the majority of medium combustion plants are operated by smes. in view of all this, the legal framework should be improved and i therefore voted in favour of the parliament's report on the proposal for a directive on this subject.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's proposal for medium combustion plants can make a significant contribution to reducing so2, nox and dust pollution by setting limits for both existing and new plants. this is a simple registration system that will help member states meet their emission reduction commitments and avoid the debate about trade-offs between quality and increased use of biomass. small combustion plants and large combustion plants are already regulated by legislation in directives and it is therefore important to also regulate emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants, which are not yet regulated at european union level.
in writing. ‒ air pollution is a cross-border problem that needs to be regulated in order to preserve health and a healthy environment. if we don't address the problem, the costs of health care and environmental protection will rise, and they will burden the economies of all nations. the directive provides for measures in the form of limits on emissions of pollutants into the air for medium combustion plants (with a heat input of 1 to 50 mw) for which a regulatory legal framework has not yet been established. it applies to both new and existing installations. the aim is primarily to reduce emissions, and regulation should not represent an increase in administrative burden for eu member states and a disproportionate burden on national economies.
in writing. ‒ the the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from medium combustion plants is part of the new eu air quality action framework set out in the revised eu thematic strategy on air pollution and is consistent with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, inclusive and sustainable growth. in fact, there are around 150 000 medium-sized combustion plants in operation in the eu, with a wide range of uses, including electricity generation, domestic heating and cooling, and the provision of heat and steam for industrial processes. i appreciate that the proposal is prepared to make a significant contribution to reducing nox, so2 and dust pollution by setting limits for new and existing installations as well as a simple registration system to help member states meet a significant part of their emission reduction commitments and to avoid possible trade-offs between quality and increased use of biomass, which could otherwise lead to increased air pollution. in doing so, the administrative burden is kept to the lowest possible level, which gives a realistic hope for the application of the directive without creating an unnecessary burden on society and the economy.

in writing. ‒ although emissions of air pollutants have decreased significantly in recent decades, we are still witnessing that air quality in many areas of the eu remains problematic and citizens are exposed to substances that potentially threaten their health and wellbeing. i therefore believe that it is our moral duty to look for new ways of bringing the union below the limits it has set itself. as there are currently around 150 000 medium combustion plants in operation in the eu, which are a significant source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust emissions, it is necessary to adopt measures to help member states reduce emissions of certain pollutants into the air. i supported the resolution because i believe that the regulation of medium-sized combustion plants with rated thermal input between 1 and 50 mw is one of the options that can create a more coherent regulatory environment and thus close the large gap in current eu legislation. at the same time, i expect the changes brought about by the report to be an important tool for improving air quality in the eu without imposing an unnecessary burden on society and the economy.

in writing. ‒ the the obligation to apply the general procurement rules of the european union to crisis management measures under the common foreign and security policy and in particular to civilian missions is significantly delaying the procurement of essential equipment and services and has a negative impact on the functioning of those missions. as a rule, missions operate in crisis environments and only for a limited period. i therefore support the proposal to introduce specific rules for such missions in crisis or post-crisis environments and to align the regulations on budgetary rules with the provisions of the new public procurement directives for external actions.
in writing. ‒ the draft financial regulation aims to amend and streamline the existing rules relating to the general budget of the union. it is now mandatory to apply the regulations and rules in the same way in all circumstances. however, these rules are not adapted to crisis and post-crisis situations where their application may have negative impacts such as delays, incomplete equipment and malfunctions within missions. it is necessary to adapt the existing eu budgetary rules and to introduce specific rules for common security and defence policy missions in order to increase their flexibility and efficiency. it is therefore appropriate to provide for greater flexibility of procedures by delegating budget implementation powers to the civilian operation commander, which will lead to efficient financial management and the protection of the financial interests of the union. i call for the budgetary measures to be aligned so that the regulations under the cfsp are adapted to the situations and conditions. however, the essence of the change in the general rules on public procurement must remain efficiency, effectiveness and, above all, transparency.
in writing. ‒ i support a resolution that will increase transparency and fairness in public procurement and the award of concessions by the eu institutions. i also welcome the extension of the criteria for exclusion from participation in public procurement by the eu institutions, such as tax fraud and tax evasion, or misappropriation of public funds.
in writing. the budgetary rules, like all other eu rules, must be respected if we are to ensure an efficient and fair functioning. where the rules are not appropriate, for example in crisis responses in third countries under the common defence and security policy, they must of course be adapted to ensure the swift and flexible execution of operations.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as it introduces measures that can increase the efficiency of the use of the european union budget and reduce the amount of fraud. but much more needs to be done to make the eu budget truly effective, as the vast majority of it still consists of euro funds and subsidies to farmers, which do more harm than good.

we were united in our efforts to improve the status of women in the labour market. three years ago this parliament adopted a report by our colleague edith bauer on the principle of equal pay for men and women for work of equal value. this report contained a list of specific recommendations for the commission to improve the position of women in employment. but three years passed, and little changed. so i have focused in my report on four things that i think are key. first, to introduce a clear definition of work of equal value in all member states. second, to improve women's access to justice. third, the motivation of employers. and fourthly, a call on the commission to take all these requirements into account in the drafting of a new directive to replace the existing one and to impose higher requirements on the member states. the concept of equal work or work of equal value has so far been introduced in only 12 of the 28 member states. in most of them, it takes into account skill, effort, responsibility and working conditions. since the voluntary introduction of this concept has not produced the expected results, i propose that it should be made compulsory in all member states, which will also contribute to the deepening of the freedom of movement of labour in the european union. these are in particular paragraphs 8, 9, 10 and 11. the definition of work of equal value is complemented by the obligation for employers to define jobs neutrally, i.e. in such a way that neither men nor women are favoured as applicants. such a requirement may require greater sensitivity, but it certainly does not represent an additional administrative burden. as regards women's access to justice, i propose strengthening anti-discrimination offices and, where appropriate, trade unions in the member states and extending their powers, even to the point of offering women not only legal advice but also representation before the courts in discrimination cases. it is the lack of legal awareness and financial situation that prevents many women from seeking justice. when i speak of employer motivation, i am thinking in particular of the recommendation in paragraph 37 that companies that do not fulfil their gender equality obligations should be excluded from public procurement of goods and services financed from the european union budget. i would like to emphasize that it is not a sanction, but a motivation. anyone who wants to apply for european contracts must create a level playing field for the men and women he employs. ladies and gentlemen, the obligation to treat everyone equally has been enshrined in the treaties of the european union for almost 60 years and it is our responsibility to ensure that every employer in the european union respects it. in recent years, we have seen stagnation. it's time to finally get over it and move on.
the report is very good at identifying a problem which i personally consider important, and that is the problem of a specific group of parents, mainly mothers, who take care of their disabled children with great love and daily physical and mental commitment. it is a great shame that caring for such children is synonymous with living in poverty and gives rise to a phenomenon known as the feminization of poverty. member states must therefore be more involved not only in rewarding this work but also in creating conditions to promote the creation of jobs for mothers who want to work at least part-time but are rejected by employers because of the health problems of their children. it is not enough to have a ban on discrimination on paper, because the reality will change only when we finally stop thinking of these women as those who are inferior in the labor market. maternity, care for the sick, the elderly and the disabled must not be a stigma and a condemnation to a low pension, but a value in itself and an equal contribution to life in our society. in writing. ‒ the draft resolution on payment services in the internal market adopted by parliament aims to complement and update the internal market regulation on payment services. parliament endorses the agreement reached between the institutions at first reading. the reforms will reduce the cost of money market services, provide consumers with free information on financial transactions, increase payment security and enable innovative new payment methods to be introduced in the market, with a view to the secure transfer of personal data. all these changes are in the interests of consumers and businesses. the development of an internal market for secure electronic payments will also allow the union economy to grow and to exploit the full potential of the internal market. i supported the report.
in writing. in the current era of globalisation, traditional trade is being transformed into a digital economy, while the offer of electronic payments to users is developing. these changes also require appropriate legislative adjustment to increase legal certainty and protection of the actors in these relationships. the proposal responds to the development of electronic and mobile transactions and the emergence of new types of payment services. the introduction of more precise rights and obligations for the individual, payment institutions and member states will contribute to the transparency and security of payment transactions, increase competition and at the same time eliminate unfair practices such as data misuse or money laundering.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the proposal for a directive on payment services in the internal market because of the continuing development of an integrated internal market, which is of great importance for promoting economic growth in the union. the key principles of full integrity and efficiency are security and transparency in payments and the use of payment services. it is therefore necessary to harmonise the market and to further strengthen consumer confidence. new rules should be established and a level playing field ensured to ensure the uniform application of the legislative framework in the eu. i consider it important to focus on providing adequate protection to consumers and businesses, who are bound by the right to know the actual cost of payments and services and to be clearly informed of their rights and obligations, with the aim of strengthening certainty towards a harmonised payment market. i appreciate the development of the integrated market and i welcome the regulations that will prevent different approaches within the internal market in order to take full advantage of the benefits it brings. the volume of electronic payments is constantly increasing and the use of new services is constantly increasing, which i see as a trend on a global scale. it is therefore necessary to recognise the need to accelerate the establishment and harmonisation of an efficient integrated payments market.
