in writing. ‒ the abolition of the death penalty worldwide is one of the main objectives of the eu's human rights policy. according to the office of the united nations high commissioner for human rights, more than 160 un member states have either abolished the death penalty or do not use it in practice. despite this, the latest figures show that in 2014, at least 2,466 people were sentenced to death in 55 countries, an increase of 23% compared to 2013. in addition, the imposition of death sentences and executions continue at an alarming rate in 2015. i particularly condemn the use of the death penalty by certain countries to crush resistance, and for reasons of religious difference or belief, homosexuality or adultery, or for any other reason which can be considered as a minor offence or not a criminal offence at all. i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution condemning the use of the death penalty and strongly supporting the introduction of a moratorium on the death penalty as a step towards its abolition, stating that the abolition of the death penalty contributes to the strengthening of human dignity and that the ultimate objective of the eu is the universal abolition of the death penalty.
in writing. ‒ on 10 october, we celebrate the world day against the death penalty, yet in 2014 alone, at least 22 countries carried out executions and at least 2 466 people were sentenced to death. in countries that still use the death penalty, dozens of europeans are facing execution. it is our duty to make every effort to abolish the death penalty at least for acts contrary to the international covenant on civil and political rights, and the death penalty should not be imposed for drug-related offences. it is important that the european external action service, the commission and the member states provide guidance for a comprehensive and effective european policy on the death penalty, with regard to the dozens of europeans facing this threat in third countries.
in writing. the use of the death penalty in the world is on a downward trend. yet, there are still countries in the world that use it as a legitimate punishment. statistics on this subject are sketchy because some countries withhold information. the execution of this punishment is often carried out in silence, without notification to the public or the family, in a humiliating and painful manner. there is no doubt that this punishment and the way it is carried out is inhumane. history has repeatedly shown that the punishment has been abused either intentionally or negligently, with irreversible and irreparable consequences. the eu and its member states reject the existence of the death penalty in the rule of law and advocate its abolition worldwide. i therefore support any initiative by the eu institutions and bodies that contributes to this.

in writing. ‒ parliament's resolution draws lessons from the red mud disaster in hungary five years ago and reiterates the need for common european solutions and cooperation in the event of environmental and industrial disasters and to prevent them. ten people lost their lives in the accident in the colony's waste storage, many were injured, the landslide that overwhelmed the areas of the affected villages caused significant environmental damage, we are talking about the worst industrial disaster in the history of hungary. the rescue and recovery efforts following the columbarium accident have become a symbol of solidarity. the resolution adopted was the result of a multiparty consensus, and i voted in favour of its text. i would like to stress that the resolution is forward-looking and calls on the european commission to continue work on the establishment of an eu disaster insurance system capable of applying the 'polluter pays' principle in the event of major industrial disasters. as long as there are no mandatory financial guarantees and the polluter is unable to compensate for the damage he has caused, the polluter pays principle cannot be applied in practice. all of this poses a risk in the event of an industrial accident. strengthening facility controls, avoiding bureaucratic constraints, and promoting the use of appropriate technologies in member states will play an important role in preventing similar disasters in the future.
in writing. the case of the october 2010 ecological disaster in hungary, when a dump of hazardous waste ruptured and caused damage to life, health and property, has raised more questions. this is the need for eu compensation for damage, but also for sufficient preventive measures in the field of hazardous waste management and the associated environmental protection. red sludge and other hazardous waste are still a risk of such environmental and industrial disasters in other eu countries. we must therefore require the commission to report on compliance with eu environmental liability standards and, on the basis of its findings, to propose new measures to strengthen the preventive effects in this area.
in writing. ‒ the collapse of a waste dam in hungary on 4 october 2010 was the last, but certainly not the only, such accident in europe in recent decades. it is therefore really necessary to learn enough and take measures to ensure that the disaster that killed 10 people and injured almost 150 in hungary five years ago is the last one to remain. moreover, its consequences did not end with this calculation. as a doctor, i would like to point out that the drying of the mud that has been left in the environment after nearly a million cubic meters of highly alkaline red mud has been deposited has produced fine dust that settles in the respiratory tract and travels up the circulatory system, potentially causing other health problems. in addition, the mud dust from the accident contained other dangerous pests. in this case, the arsenic content is particularly dangerous, as it can cause oncological disease if it enters the lungs. as the accident has shown the inadequate implementation of eu law, the deficiencies in inspections and the gaps in the relevant eu legislation, i join my colleagues in asking the commission: what lessons have been learned from this accident?
in writing. ‒ the tragic events of 4 october 2010, when a waste tank with bauxite sludge from aluminium production ruptured, marked the entire surroundings of the affected area of vesprém county. i therefore appreciate the fact that the european parliament is returning to this event in order to improve the remediation of the damage that still persists after the accident. that's why i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ the the issue of roaming has been around for several years. in 2012, a regulation of the european parliament and of the council was adopted which set the political objective of gradually harmonising charges for mobile communications at home and abroad, i.e. abolishing the roaming surcharge. under that regulation, roaming should end on 15 june 2017. we have now adopted a new regulation in parliament which introduces a transitional period between the current situation and the total ban on roaming surcharges. during this period, the maximum eu-wide roaming surcharges will be further reduced, starting from april 2016. this means that customers will not pay more than 5 cents per minute for a mobile phone call from abroad, sms will not cost more than 2 cents and 1 megabyte of data transferred will also cost a maximum of 5 cents. however, mobile operators will be able to apply a 'fair user policy'. this should prevent, for example, customers who have moved permanently to another member state from using roaming during this transitional period. in such cases, operators will be able to charge the customer a small additional fee, but this fee will not be higher than the maximum wholesale margin between operators. the threshold for the 'fair user policy' will be defined by the commission by 15 december 2015.
in writing, the directive on taxation of savings in the european union was adopted in 2003 and entered into force in 2005. in march 2015, the european commission presented a tax transparency package and, as part of this package, proposed the repeal of the 2003 savings tax directive. the european commission wants to remove the burden on member states to avoid having to apply the provisions of both directives and to avoid a double system in the collection of information and data. the abolition of the savings tax directive is possible if the european commission acts, if necessary, through legislative proposals, to ensure that the risk of loss of tax revenue for member states in the european union is reduced.
in writing, the council and the commission must give careful consideration to the practical implications, in particular if there is a risk of loss of tax revenue for the member states of the union, when proposing repeal. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposal that the commission report on the consequences of the repeal of the savings tax directive in relation to the bridging period until 2017, when the international exchange of information will take effect, and that the commission ensure, through legislative proposals, that any losses are excluded.
‒ the fight against tax evasion and the need for fair taxation is a major issue at european but also global level. as far back as 2003, the eu savings tax directive was adopted as a measure to ensure that savings interest is taxed. the directive has been applied in the eu countries and in separate agreements between the eu countries and the 12 overseas territories. in parallel, bilateral agreements were also concluded with five european countries outside the eu. in the meantime, the 2011 administrative cooperation directive has been revised to align it with the oecd global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information in tax matters, which will apply from 1 january 2016. as part of the march 2015 tax transparency package, the commission proposes to repeal the savings tax directive so that member states do not have to apply the provisions of both directives in order to avoid the complexity of double data collection and transmission systems. as the administrative cooperation directive has a much wider scope, i support the repeal of the savings income tax directive.

in writing ‒ the european parliament, on the basis of a report, gives a discharge to the director of the eit in respect of the implementation of the institute's budget for the financial year 2013, but the parliament made its observations in a resolution before forwarding the decision. in 2013, the eit failed to certify, for the second consecutive year, the legality and regularity report on its grant operations to the court of auditors. i am therefore pleased that the quality of the institute's audit certificates has improved since 2014 following the guidance of the court of auditors. the eit has improved its budget implementation procedures and introduced additional controls for grant operations to ensure a higher degree of assurance of legality and regularity. following the fulfilment of the conditions and instructions issued by the court of auditors, parliament approved the eit's accounts for the financial year 2013 and granted discharge.
in writing. ‒ i voted in accordance with the principle that discharge for any part of the eu budget should follow only after the eu budget as a whole has received a favourable opinion from the european court of auditors.
in writing, the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013, has, for the second consecutive year, not found that there is reasonable assurance as to the legality and regularity of the institute's grant operations. according to the court, the quality of the good practices is in question as they are issued by independent audit firms hired by the grant recipients themselves and which cover approximately 87% of the grant expenditure. it is therefore good that the institute has introduced additional ex post controls for grant operations as a second level of assurance on the legality and regularity of grant operations. the institute also carried out 'on-the-spot' audits of around 40% of the grants paid under the 2013 grant agreements. the institute has improved its procurement procedures since 2013 and has taken a proactive approach following the court's findings of errors. the institute improved its budget implementation planning and monitoring procedures and took further necessary measures to improve its overall management. that is why i voted to discharge the institute for 2013.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the activities of the european institute of innovation and technology, because innovation and technology are an important part of our economy and only thanks to them can our economy thrive and compete with other world powers.
in writing. ‒ the eniac joint undertaking has addressed the problems identified in the first discharge report in a meaningful manner, as assessed by the budgetary control committee, and has reinforced the application of the conflict of interest rules. thanks to that, the panel decided to grant the discharge, to close the accounts. that is why i supported the granting of the discharge to the eniac joint undertaking.

in writing. ‒ the parliament's report draws lessons from the ebola crisis in africa in 2014. the ebola outbreak in sierra leone, liberia and guinea in march 2014 was the largest such crisis to date, posing a challenge to the african region concerned, but also to the international community and to european countries involved in the crisis management. the report looks ahead to prevent and respond to epidemics with high loss of life. to this end, the eu should strive to improve health systems in the future. it is necessary to lay down the conditions for a permanent european system with adequate material and human resources for immediate response. investing in health promotes economic development and is thus an important factor in poverty eradication. the report calls on member states to contribute to the establishment of the universal health fund (uhc) and hopes that the european development fund will also support the health systems of countries with fragile infrastructure through its investments. i supported the adoption of the report, in line with the aims of the report and the line of the people's party.
‒ sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been battling the worst ebola crisis in history since march 2014. it is clear that these three countries are not able to cope with the epidemic on their own and the people of these countries are placed in an extremely vulnerable situation. as a world leader in development, the european union has a special responsibility in establishing and improving the healthcare system in the countries concerned. if we are to successfully fight the ebola epidemic, it is very important that we also think about health development, investment in health and economic development in the affected countries. cooperation between the european union and the african countries concerned can only succeed if they develop rapidly in the economic and health sectors.
‒ the current extent of the ebola infectious disease epidemic in the african countries sierra leone, liberia and guinea demonstrates that these countries, given their economic and financial situation and, in particular, the state of their social and health services, are not able to cope with the situation without the assistance of other countries. it is therefore appropriate to review and redirect eu financial assistance to developing countries so that the funds provided are targeted at addressing the country's problems and are not misused for other undesirable purposes. to this end, measures should be taken to enhance control over the management of the aid provided and to allow timely intervention.
in writing. ‒ the in march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea were hit by the worst ebola outbreak in history, and i therefore welcome the resolution on this crisis and consider it important to learn from it for the future. since time is of the essence, it is now necessary to identify the shortcomings in the health-care system there. if the european parliament recognises that women were more affected by ebola in these countries, accounting for 55 to 75% of the victims, let us address what led to this. they make up the majority of the medical staff, but the system lacks basic medical and protective equipment. worse still, even in areas not affected by ebola, fear of infection has caused people to refuse even routine medical treatment. women even stopped giving birth in hospitals. this has resulted in an increasing number of non-ebola-related deaths of women and children. i therefore call on europe to help these countries develop their own public health systems and infrastructure to ensure that all citizens have access to them. but let us not make part of the funding conditional on the focus on sexual and reproductive rights, as the resolution mentions, especially if they are understood only as access to contraception and abortion.
in writing. - i welcome the report. the european union must do everything possible to prevent a major epidemiological disaster of this magnitude in the future. lessons to be learned from the ebola epidemic it is very important to make international crisis management more effective. a quick response is therefore essential, for life is worth time. the ebola epidemic has had other long-term consequences besides the loss of thousands of lives. for example, the increase in orphans the huge number of children who have lost their parents, but their relatives are afraid to take them in because of the possibility of infection. affected children are often rejected from school, which can mean a complete break in their education. and in developing countries, education is the most important thing. we can't turn our backs on emergency relief. we're talking about countries where the population lacks basic hygiene practices. without proper water supply and sanitation, the spread of viral diseases cannot be prevented. the marshall plan can help develop a health and education system that can meet basic needs. we must not forget the measures we can take here in europe. this is what research and development can be, because the more we know about ebola and other viral diseases, the closer we are to developing antibodies.

in writing. the increase in the number of judges at the court of justice of the european union has been on the agenda for several years in order to deal more effectively with the constantly increasing number of cases. this proposal shall apply to the judges of the general court in the court of justice. the european council and the european parliament reached a compromise on the issue in the 2014 european parliament elections, and the european parliament adopted its own position on the issue in 2014. in september 2014, the italian presidency in the council requested a new draft proposal from the court of justice, because the member states could not agree on a system for the selection of judges, the proposed 12 judges could not have been appointed on a fair, national basis. the new proposal resulted in an agreement between the member states in the council, which was adopted by parliament's legal affairs committee. it provides for a gradual increase in the number of judges to a total of 56 and for a balance between the sexes and the nationalities to be maintained. this proposal was put to the plenary. the decision contains a review clause, which requires an impact assessment to be carried out after 5 years to assess whether the proposed solution fulfils the expectations, i.e. the processing of the backlog in order to achieve a balanced, rapid and professional legislation. as written, i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the eu points to the increasing average length of proceedings before the general court. it argues that the current number of 28 judges (one judge per country appointed by government agreement for six years) is not sufficient. the council therefore proposed to increase the number of judges to 56, two for each member state. this request came at a time when the eu institutions had agreed to reduce their staff by 5% and their expenditure by 0.5%. no proper legislative proposal has been submitted in this case, no consultative body has commented on the proposal, no analyses and impact assessments have been carried out. the number of judges has been increased by the number of judges appointed by the president of the republic. the court of justice has also been the subject of a number of judgments, including one in the general court, which was delivered in may 2014. it will be necessary to monitor the statistics of this institution on a regular basis and to evaluate productivity.
in writing. ‒ the speed of judicial proceedings before the court of justice of the eu appears to be decreasing and the number of pending cases to be increasing, due to the gradual expansion of jurisdiction and the number of cases brought. however, before considering the very complex question of increasing or even doubling the number of judges on the court, it is necessary to consider appropriate and effective measures, both from a procedural and organisational point of view. i therefore support the proposal to set up a joint committee of experts to examine the general functioning of the union judiciary and to make proposals for its improvement.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the proposed increase in the number of judges of the general court and therefore did not support the proposal. the proposed increase in the number of judges is purely political and has no rational justification and, moreover, increases expenditure by eur 20 million per year, instead of striving for budgetary neutrality.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report on the request of the european court of justice to increase the number of judges for the general court. although the reasons given by the court for its request, namely to reduce the burden on individual judges of the number of cases and thus to speed up the procedure, are understandable, i do not share the idea of supporting a proposal whose implications have not yet been examined. no independent study has been carried out to assess the need for the requested change. in my view, an impact study should be the basis for any objective decision on proposals.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as it mainly involves technical changes.
in writing. ‒ the new proposal from the european commission to the european parliament for the use of genetically modified food and feed follows a non-gmo policy, which would allow member states to ban the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. despite the remaining shortcomings in the proposal, the european commission's proposal should not be rejected, but negotiations should be continued in a constructive spirit. the cooperative approach was also the basis for the creation of the law on the prohibition of public farming. if we don't give this proposal a chance to be debated, we may miss an opportunity that will not be followed by another. i did not support the report by mr la via rejecting the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ the genetically modified food and feed may be placed on the market for sale to consumers only if an additional authorisation has been granted. the tasks of the european commission and the member states are clearly defined in the existing legal framework of the european union. member states have been allowed to restrict or prohibit, under certain conditions, the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after those products have been authorised. such measures must be compatible with the internal market and the international commitments of the european union. in particular, national measures must be justified and based on compelling reasons which must not be contrary to a risk assessment. member states must provide substantial grounds justifying their exemption, while respecting the internal market rules and wto trade rules, in order to provide the necessary legal certainty and adequate tools for member states wishing to legally restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation appears confusing and could give rise to legal uncertainty because of the already existing arrangements, which also include the necessary measures of the member states and the commission in the field of gmos. the original regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 established a system in this area. it regulates the use and authorisation procedure of gmos on the markets of the member states in such a way that they do not pose a risk to human or animal health or the environment. it takes account of the eu's position as the largest importer of agricultural products. however, the placing on the market of gmos is preceded by a scientific risk assessment, the responsibility for which lies with the european food safety authority (efsa) in cooperation with the scientific bodies of the member states. this regulation also lays down measures that member states or the commission may take against the placing or use of gmos where the product is likely to present a risk to health and life. also in march 2015, a directive of the european parliament and of the council (eu) was adopted allowing member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their territory.
in writing. ‒ however, the use of genetically modified food and feed is a matter of caution, mainly because we cannot yet say with certainty whether it will be beneficial to humanity. it should be said that the european union has the strictest regulation of genetically modified food in the world. it is therefore unnecessary to introduce regulations allowing member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. moreover, the conditions for granting an exemption, which have been in force until now, have never been fulfilled. the safeguard clause has been invoked by states in nine cases so far, but in all these cases the eu scientific committees found that there were no grounds to change the original authorisation decision. moreover, the proposed regulation is almost impossible to implement as there are no longer any border controls within the eu agricultural sector. the reintroduction of such controls between member states would reverse the economic achievements of the european customs union and the single market. in addition, the dependence of union livestock production on genetically modified feed should be taken into account. the adoption of the regulation could result in a reduction of production in the eu and thus the need to import from countries with lower animal production standards than the union.
in writing. ‒ i am fundamentally in favour of the ambition that individual member states should have the right to decide whether they want to see food and feed containing gmos within their borders. in this case, however, i voted against the european commission's proposal. the commission has therefore decided to initiate the procedure laid down in article 93 (2) of the treaty in respect of the application of the principle of proportionality. for example, there is no impact assessment of the consequences of member states' decisions, and the proposal is practically unfeasible in its current form, as it is extremely difficult to prevent gm crops from entering the market in europe with today's air borders, once they are already on the market in a member state. i expect the european commission to put forward a more precise proposal.
in writing. ‒ i consider genetically modified food and feed to be experimentation and i am against their cultivation in slovakia. at eu level, i think it is important that each eu country has the opportunity to decide on this issue independently. however, i did not consider the content of the proposal submitted, concerning the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory, to be sufficiently satisfactory and therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ genetically modified foods are highly controversial, and even among scientists there is no consensus on the subject. member states must therefore be free to decide whether or not to authorise their cultivation and sale on their territory.
in writing. - i supported the motion. i fully agree that the decision to use or not to use gmos is a matter for the member states themselves. however, i also share the rapporteur's view that the commission's current proposal contains fundamental problems and should therefore be recast.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the commission's proposal to revert to the restriction or ban on the marketing of gmos at national level, as this would have been a major step backwards in the field. in addition to the differences it would have created between member states, such a proposal would have had a catastrophic consequence: the weakening of the single market. the commission will therefore have to come back with a new proposal, one which is more in line with the expectations of european citizens and which does not undermine one of the foundations of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on this report. the commission proposal itself was complicated and in my view the vote did not allow for a clear statement of the position of members on genetically modified food. at the beginning of this year, we voted that member states should be able to ban the cultivation of genetically modified crops on their territory. i agree with this position and, given the diversity of views on this watched and controversial topic and the fact that the consequences of gmos on human health and the environment are not yet sufficiently studied, member states should not be denied the possibility to decide whether or not to grow, or place or not place on the market, genetically modified food as they consider necessary or risky for their populations.

in writing. ‒ the parliament's report supports the european commission's proposal for emission limit values for the six main air pollutants, namely nitrogen oxides, ammonia and methane, to be applied by member states. the eu's new emissions targets are a step in the right direction, and the eu is committed to achieving a high level of emissions reductions by 2020.
in writing. ‒ poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths each year and the economic value to health systems in individual member states is in the range of 300-900 billion each year. more than 90% of the population living in cities in the member states of the european union are exposed to air pollution that is harmful to their health. in addition, the most vulnerable groups of the population, such as pregnant women, children and the elderly, as well as low-income groups, are also exposed to these negative impacts.
in writing. ‒ the directive provides a framework for the adoption of measures and regulations in eu countries' regimes to achieve climate change mitigation, air quality, public health and environmental improvements, which are among the union's long-term objectives. many member states do not comply with the standards and commitments they have made so far, delaying the achievement of the targets. this results in a deterioration in the health of the population and increases health care spending. the directive repeals and replaces the existing directive on national emission ceilings, sets measures for individual sectors and sectors of economic life and sets new emission ceilings for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and non-methane volatile organic compounds for 2020 and 2030. from 2020, it shall also apply to particulate matter. in order not to increase the cost of adopting the targets set, it will be necessary to focus on new and innovative ways of financing emission reductions.
in writing. ‒ the european air policy has a long history and has made significant progress, but the eu is still far from its long-term goal of meeting the recommended pollutant limits set out in the 2005 who air quality guidelines. i therefore welcome the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants. the aim must be to achieve air quality levels that do not have unacceptable impacts and risks to human health and the environment. today, poor air quality contributes to premature deaths, sickness absences, high healthcare costs and lost productivity, with the total external health-related costs to companies from air pollution estimated at between eur 330 and 940 billion per year. moreover, according to the oecd, by 2050, urban air pollution may become the leading environmental cause of death worldwide.
in writing. ‒ the right to clean air should be taken for granted. however, we must strike the right balance between protecting the environment and the objective of restoring industrial production, boosting economic growth and increasing employment.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) is the first instrument of direct participatory democracy in the eu, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. the epc, better known by its acronym eci, is governed by a regulation, on which parliament has drawn up a report, taking account of the lessons learned in the first three years since its entry into force. as the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on petitions on the report to parliament, i have drawn up proposals which seek to overcome the limitations which have become apparent in practice. the instrument exists, but it must be acknowledged that it has so far been more of a disappointment than a success for eu citizens who want to participate actively in the union's activities. the technical, data-requesting parts of the regulation need to be simplified, and the fact that parliament is continuously informed by the commission of the citizens' initiatives received in order to ensure a balance between the institutions can also improve the effective functioning of the instrument. one of the main things and a call to the european commission to prepare for the revision of the regulation is to make it as easy as possible for eu citizens to access information on the citizens' initiative in more places and in more languages, preferably in their own language. the creation of the european citizens' initiative was a political decision, and it requires a strong political will to be able to take place and to function, which is why i voted in favour of the schöpflin report.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is a tool that the european parliament has been dealing with since the early stages of its development. it is a great pity that the use of this institution by the citizens of the european union is decreasing year by year, given that 16 more such initiatives were registered in 2012, in 2015 it is only one. citizens and organisers of citizens' initiatives most often encounter obstacles and lack of support and awareness from society. the different conditions and forms for signing initiatives in the different member states of the european union remain a serious problem.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative did not fulfil its objective of increasing the activity of civil society and strengthening european citizenship, especially at transnational level. none of its 51 activities has led to legislation. the implementation of the european citizens' initiative activities has encountered a number of obstacles, which could however be overcome with appropriate administrative support. i therefore support the proposal that the commission, on the basis of past experience and knowledge, should undertake a revision of the european citizens' initiative regulation in order to remove obstacles and ensure transparency and institutional balance in the decision-making process, so as to provide greater support and assistance to this activity.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative was supposed to be a tool for european citizens to participate in public affairs and to strengthen their european citizenship, but unfortunately this tool has not yet fulfilled its objectives. i therefore consider it important to adopt a resolution on a european citizens' initiative which will change this situation so that citizens' opinions are never ignored again, as happened in the case of the one of us initiative, which calls for brussels to stop funding any practices that destroy human life before birth. the former manuel barroso commission vetoed it, despite it being supported by two million people in europe and becoming the largest petition in european history. the commission thus made a farce of the european citizens' initiative, while meps, on the contrary, wanted it to become a real instrument of participatory democracy. this commission decision was contrary to ethical and democratic requirements, so i welcome the fact that the european parliament recognises that the eu institutions and member states must take all necessary steps to support the european citizens' initiative and to deepen citizens' trust in this instrument, and that it regrets the lack of legislative impact and the dissuasive actions of the commission following up on successful initiatives.
in writing. ‒ i believe that strengthening participatory democracy is the key to europe's future, the guarantee of development. if we look at the evolution of democracy, from the ancient greek example of privileged people to the modern day example of the principle of universal participation, i think the path forward is clear. it's not enough to drag citizens to the ballot box. they need to be given much more power to make their voices heard, and if they are not, then the frustration will lead to demotivation, and fewer and fewer people will vote as a result. this participatory democracy is reinforced by the institutions of petitioning and citizens' initiative. i think the legislator's intention was clear when he regulated the latter. the system still doesn't work. the european commission seemed to fear that its comfortable bureaucratic system could be invaded from outside and that the right of initiative might be taken away from ordinary citizens. he doesn't like it when almost two million people line up for an initiative like the right to water initiative. this situation is untenable and the solution to the problem cannot be delayed. the delay increases the frustration and mistrust of brussels. i hope that this report will help us take concrete steps in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is a unique and innovative instrument of participatory democracy in the eu. it allows citizens to become an active part of the processes that affect them. i am convinced that this is another way of involving our citizens more in public affairs. it is important to simplify the way european citizens' initiatives work and also to increase awareness.
in writing. - i supported the motion. i agree with the measures presented, which can make the current possibility of a european citizens' initiative more effective and give it more weight. this is also one way of increasing the democratic decision-making capacity of eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ while the european citizens' initiative is a legal instrument of direct democracy in the european union, designed to allow citizens of the european union to be directly involved in the creation of new legislation on topics they consider important, the fate of previous citizens' initiatives suggests otherwise. of the 51 initiatives launched, only 3 were able to meet the requirements and unfortunately none of them led to a legislative proposal submitted by the european commission. i think that in this situation it is appropriate to ask what is the reason for the failure of so many civic initiatives. whether it's lack of awareness of the possibility, too complex or incomprehensible requirements, or other reasons. the report looks at the possible causes and also looks at how to make this legal instrument more serious so as to restore the confidence of the citizens of the european union in its effectiveness. i consider the views of at least one million european citizens on a given subject to be of such importance that they cannot simply and unjustifiably be ignored, or be ignored on the grounds that they do not meet overly burdensome administrative requirements. that's why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the adriatic and ionian region is home to over 70 million people and covers eight countries, including four eu member states, three candidate countries and bosnia and herzegovina as a potential candidate country. i voted in favour of the draft report in the plenary vote, as eusair provides a good opportunity for the countries of the region to promote sustainable development. the pillars and other priorities of the strategy promote economic development and job creation, which in turn contribute to the stability of the region.

in writing. ‒ crossborder cooperation is a fundamental concept of the european union and the promotion and support of such cooperation. macro-regional cooperation is one of the most compelling forms of this. after two successful strategies for the baltic sea and danube regions, it seems clear that this project will be extended and additional macro-regions created. the adriatic and ionian macro-region, like the previous two, comprises a single geographical region which can clearly benefit from the single treatment. for the countries involved, this cooperation can bring many positive benefits, such as improved international relations, closer political cooperation, and specialisation in certain political and economic sectors. in the case of eusair, this macro-regional cooperation can contribute significantly to the multilateral development of countries not yet members of the eu and to closer cooperation with the eu. the strategy is broadly detailed in all four pillars and clearly covers the areas specific to the region and necessary for development. however, to ensure that the whole project does not lose its meaning, it is necessary to avoid the emergence of an unnecessary bureaucratic system and, at the same time, to insist on the establishment and maintenance of a multi-level governance of the macro-region based on the principle of subsidiarity, since local and regional actors are the most effective actors in matters affecting the region and their cooperation with other higher-level institutions can be the basis for the effective functioning of the region.

in writing. ‒ the the european commission's anticipated air transport package comes at a time when the sector is facing a number of challenges. european airports and airlines are exposed to competition from third countries, which subsidise their carriers at the expense of eu companies. the eu's air transport needs a strong stimulus to create the conditions for a sustainable and competitive environment for airlines and airports. i therefore support the resolution of parliament calling on the commission to support innovative measures in the areas of air traffic management, alternative fuels, aircraft engines and airport safety. in addition, it cannot be forgotten that the aviation industry, as a fast-growing sector, attracts highly motivated employees. however, their working conditions do not always meet european social standards, as airlines also reduce their operating costs through atypical employment contracts which put the employee at a disadvantage in many respects. it is worth noting that the number of passengers in air transport is constantly increasing and that this sector has become an important part of the european economy in recent decades. the aviation sector today employs 5.1 million people in the eu and contributes €365 billion to european gdp. it is therefore important that the commission removes the barriers that hinder the development of air transport. at the same time, however, it is essential to protect the employees who are held hostage by the airlines in this competitive battle for the passenger.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament's directive has been revised mainly for the sake of clarity, but also for better consumer protection. it aims at minimum harmonisation and thus allows member states to retain the original provisions or introduce more stringent ones at their own discretion, but the primary objective should be the protection of customers consumers. in particular, the aim is to ensure the same level of protection for the customer purchasing the insurance product and to extend the scope of this directive not only to insurance undertakings and their intermediaries but also to other market participants selling insurance products as an ancillary activity.
in writing. ‒ the the directive aims to harmonise national provisions in the insurance distribution activity, since to ensure effective protection and non-discrimination it is necessary to ensure a level playing field between service distributors, mutual recognition of knowledge and enhance customer confidence in the internal market. the directive applies to persons engaged in the provision of insurance or reinsurance to third parties and to persons whose activity consists in the provision of information on insurance contracts. member states are free to maintain or introduce more stringent provisions aimed at protecting customers and consumers, given that the directive is intended to lay down minimum obligations to be observed in the provision of information to customers by service distributors. i am positive that the adoption of the directive should not be a burden for small and medium-sized distributors.
in writing. ‒ in voting on the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on insurance intermediation, i voted in favour of adopting this resolution. in fact, it is very difficult for consumers to navigate the complex system of insurance companies and their intermediaries nowadays. the aim of this proposal for a directive is to help consumers in this area. the directive will guarantee that the client is provided with basic information about the contract, irrespective of the form of the mediation, and that the clients are also informed of the type of remuneration for the mediator, the amount and form of which can no longer be secret.
in writing. ‒ the the aim of this amendment to the insurance intermediation directive is to increase consumer protection by giving them access to more detailed information on insurance products. i therefore support the proposal for a directive of the ep and the council which will impose certain minimum information and advice requirements on dealers. under the new rules, insurance intermediaries will have to register with the competent authorities of the member states and provide clients with all the information on the costs of the insurance contract in advance. brokers and dealers should also have at their disposal, inter alia, financial reserves to be able to satisfy the claims of clients, where necessary. this directive should make the insurance market more transparent, transparent and accessible to the customer. the seller shall be obliged in all circumstances to provide comprehensible information on the type of insurance, the obligations arising from the contract, the insurance risks, the exemptions, or the method of payment for the insurance. for contracts to be beneficial for both parties, the seller and the customer, it is first and foremost necessary that the customer is not exposed to surprises which could have been avoided.
in writing. ‒ detailed and truthful consumer information is particularly important when it comes to insurance products. the directive we have approved sets minimum common standards that every intermediary must meet and will clear the market of quick-witted experts in the world of finance.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the proposal as it increases the regulatory burden and thus damages the business environment. while the increased regulatory burden is intended to protect the customer, the deterioration of the business environment in the insurance intermediation sector will inevitably come at the expense of restricting competition, which will ultimately also harm the customer itself.
in writing. ‒ i supported the new directive because it will increase consumer protection. it will also make it easier for the customer to buy insurance products. the rules adopted will apply across the eu and will guarantee that dealers and intermediaries provide the same minimum level of information and advice. this will better protect consumers, whether before the conclusion of the contract or in the event of problems arising in the provision of insurance benefits, for example because the intermediary, through his negligence, causes the insurance undertaking not to have to provide such benefits.
in writing. ‒ the draft directive on insurance intermediation concerns all insurance providers and intermediaries. in practice, this means in particular greater clarity, information and protection for the consumer. i consider providing clear, understandable and non-misleading information to be an important step in protecting clients. for example, the consumer will now be assured that he will be provided with sufficient information to make an informed decision and that he will be provided with protection in the event of a dispute, including with a foreign provider. it will also ensure that insurance intermediaries have expertise in the products they recommend and that their expertise is monitored by the member states. i hope that this measure will prevent the current proliferation of various unqualified intermediaries and advisers. another important benefit for consumers is that they will no longer be able to force insurance on them when they buy a product. finally, i also welcome provisions that should ensure that insurance providers no longer condition the remuneration of intermediaries by recommending specific products that are most profitable for them but do not meet the needs of the client. this will give the client greater assurance that the product offered to him corresponds as closely as possible to his requirements and has not been selected for him solely in the interest of a higher remuneration of the intermediary. all of these elements convinced me to support the report.

in writing. ‒ i support the ep's opinion calling on the commission to withdraw its implementing decision and to submit a new proposal rejecting the application for authorisation for a composition of recycled soft pvc containing dehp. dehp is present in many types of pvc widely used in everyday consumer products such as textiles, furniture and building materials. this substance is chemically bound to plastics, and therefore easily leaks into the environment. however, caution should be exercised in the use of dehp as current scientific evidence suggests that exposure to these compounds during the sensitive period may have serious effects on human health, in particular may have serious effects on reproduction. in addition, adverse effects on human life caused by exposure during the early life stages may not manifest until later in life. phthalates known to be endocrine disrupting and toxic to reproduction should not be present in products that are freely available to the public and may be encountered by children. the commission is also responsible for protecting citizens and the environment from dangerous chemicals. it is therefore inconceivable that innovation in product manufacturing should take precedence over human health.

in writing. ‒ speculation, tax havens, tax evasion, fraud, speculative capital movements are costing every european citizen hundreds of euros a year. european countries lose more than a trillion euros a year. individual tax policies disadvantage other economies. the solution is common procedures. if a country does not cooperate, the commission must intervene. the tax systems of the member states differ considerably in terms of the tax base and the tax rate. while tax policy is a priority area of national competence, cross-border trade, the free movement of capital and labour, globalisation and the digitalisation of trade and markets will require some key tax policy issues to be set by the eu. structural changes in the member states and the eu therefore need to include a fair, balanced and transparent reform of tax systems.
in writing. ‒ the the globalisation of the economy is changing the way individual markets work. the majority of companies are now multinational in nature and structure, thus going beyond the scope of national tax rules. a fair tax policy needs to be introduced as part of the structural reforms of the member states. the uncoordinated tax framework is the result of insufficient cooperation between member states. improvement could be achieved through automatic and systematic exchange of information, but the current monitoring framework is not effective because the requirements are not being met. inconsistencies between tax systems at global level are the cause of distortions of the tax base and result in significant tax evasion. i stress that action at union level alone will not be sufficient to address these issues. i welcome the commission's commitment to promote automatic exchange of information as the future european and international standard for transparency. tax rulings should aim to provide legal certainty, improve transparency and enhance cooperation between member states in tax policy at union level. i am of the opinion that the member states should retain full power to set their own corporate tax rates. however, i insist that tax competition within the eu and with third countries should be governed by a clear framework of rules to guarantee fair competition between companies in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ multinational companies often exploit current legislative adjustments to tax policy to adjust their taxable profits and reduce their overall tax burden. it is important to combat these practices. at the same time, however, this situation must not be misused to promote the eu's common tax policy, which is the exclusive competence of the member states. i therefore had to vote against this motion in the resolution on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect.
in writing. ‒ the recent luxleaks scandal has brought the public's attention to the aggressive tax planning practices of large multinationals. the disclosures that corporations use tax transactions that allow them to pay almost no taxes are not new, but after this scandal it was possible to point to specific companies and specific practices. the european parliament has therefore set up a special committee of inquiry which has now produced its report, containing all the most important measures to prevent such dubious tax operations. i am convinced that the existing corporate tax models, which date back to the first half of the 20th century, are not suitable for today's globalised and digitalised economy, as most large companies today have a multinational structure. i therefore support the proposals which, according to the results of the inquiry, should lead to a limitation of corporate tax deductions. the commission should first conclude the legislative form of a common consolidated corporate tax base at pan-european level. it is also necessary to establish a central register for the exchange of information on tax rulings between countries and a european list of tax havens. last but not least, european legislation should better protect whistleblowers, as they are the only ones who can help to uncover such cases. i hope that the work of the committee will continue, because tax avoidance is a problem that we will encounter regularly in a globalised world.
in writing. ‒ we must do everything possible to combat tax evasion and fraud as effectively as possible, but at the same time we must reject any attempt to limit the tax sovereignty of the member states. the whole european economy would suffer greatly.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the proposal because i do not agree with steps that facilitate or even directly lead to tax harmonisation in the european union. genuine competition between tax systems is essential for the competitiveness of the european union.
in writing. ‒ slovakia is a country that suffers from tax evasion by large companies on the one hand, but on the other hand has a weak infrastructure, so it has to offer investors tax incentives to create jobs here. our interest therefore lies in the intersection between eliminating tax evasion and fraud and preserving the tax sovereignty of the member states. i therefore support the harmonisation of tax terminology in the eu, as well as the introduction of an obligation for multinational companies to provide profit and tax data for each country in which they operate. decisions on their taxation in the individual member states must not be subject to secrecy. however, i have doubts about the need to introduce a common consolidated corporate tax base i believe that such a move should be preceded by a professional discussion of its implications for less developed member states.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report on the cases of favourable tax agreements between luxembourg and large multinationals. while i condemn the practice of states concluding agreements with large companies in order to increase their attractiveness to multinational companies and thus their competitive advantage in tax competition, i refuse to support the idea that to prevent such practices tax harmonisation at european level is necessary, including mandatory consolidated corporate income tax or a common definition of a minimum tax rate.

in writing. ‒ the recently, eu citizens have become increasingly sensitive to animal welfare. since it is important that citizens have the possibility to decide what food they will consume, the commission should proceed to develop a common strategy concerning the conditions under which animals are kept. i therefore agree with the ep's opinion, which calls on the commission to take into account the latest scientific research showing shortcomings in the housing conditions to which animals are exposed. european legislation, in its current form, is too fragmented and creates legal uncertainty that puts producers at a disadvantage and does not provide sufficient certainty for consumers. it is therefore necessary to harmonise animal welfare rules taking into account new scientific findings. however, the commission should first of all bear in mind that animals are often kept for mass production in conditions that are inhumane. animal welfare should be further improved on the basis of the prevailing scientific knowledge and with due regard to the efficiency and competitiveness of livestock farming. a high standard of animal welfare is important for ensuring sustainability, although it is associated with investments and additional operating costs.

in writing. ‒ the un estimates that one billion children live in conflict-affected areas, where they are denied the basic right to education by not being able to attend school or by having to interrupt school for long periods because of conflict or crisis. children and young people who have not attended or stopped attending school face many risks, ranging from poverty, loss of future opportunities for adequate employment, to the threat of exploitation, trafficking or recruitment into terrorist or extremist groups. i am convinced that education also plays a crucial role in the long-term reconstruction of post-conflict societies, as it offers the prospect of better integration into the workplace and thus the possibility of breaking out of poverty while contributing to economic growth. otherwise, the lack of education and positive opportunities leads to deepening frustration and discontent, which are the breeding ground for criminal and anti-social activities, violence and extremism. i therefore support eu investment in education in emergencies and fragile conditions and commend the meritorious work of all humanitarian and development actors working closely together on the important link between aid, recovery and development.

in writing. ‒ relations between the european union and the dominican republic are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part (the cotonou agreement), as well as by the celaceu dialogue and the eucariforum dialogue. the dominican republic has become one of the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. the agreement was signed in brussels on 28 may 2015. the agreement has since been applied on a provisional basis, pending the european parliament's approval, which it has now given. the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and for citizens of the dominican community for travel to the territory of the other contracting party for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (both private, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders) and to travel for any purpose other than the pursuit of a gainful activity. the agreement will boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment links. visa liberalisation will simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and enhance economic links between businesses.

in writing. ‒ the eu-saint vincent and the grenadines visa liberalisation agreement reflects the successful relationship that has been developing since saint vincent and the grenadines' independence. the situation in the country has not always been the easiest, especially due to natural disasters that have affected the export of the most important agricultural product, bananas. however, the country is now experiencing positive developments and economic recovery, with the country beginning to focus on tourism, external trade and social development. the conclusion of the agreement will provide an opportunity for cooperation on human rights, the achievement of the sustainable development goals and the strengthening of relations. the main objective, however, will be to give a new impetus to ongoing trade and exchanges between the two parties.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and saint vincent and the grenadines on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement offers an excellent opportunity to boost tourism, facilitate investment and boost trade, thereby increasing the importance of economic and cultural links between the european union and the aforementioned state. in addition, the agreement offers new allies to join forces on major issues such as the fight against terrorism. we also welcome the emergence of political dialogue, most often aimed at joint action against corruption, criminal organisations and trafficking in human beings.

in writing. ‒ eu-uae relations are conducted within the framework of the 1988 cooperation agreement between the eu and the gulf cooperation council. the european union opened a mission in the uae in 2013, demonstrating its willingness to strengthen bilateral cooperation. the united arab emirates has been included among the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. the agreement was signed in brussels on 6 may 2015 and has now been given the necessary approval by the european parliament. the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and citizens of the uae for travel to the territory of the other contracting party for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the uae is the first arab country with which the european union has signed a visa waiver agreement. more than 150 000 european citizens are settled in the uae, with some 1,6 million european visitors a year. in 2014, around 230 000 uae nationals travelled to europe, mainly for business or luxury tourism. the eu is the main trading partner of the uae in terms of trade relations and the uae is ranked 14th among the trading partners of the union and its member states, and the visa waiver could further boost economic relations.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, the continuation of the global financial and economic crisis or the new global financial and economic crisis, and to assist them with their reintegration into the labour market. on 12 june 2015, finland submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in 69 enterprises active in the computer programming, consultancy and related services sectors. finland requested a financial contribution of eur 2,623 million, which would be for 1200 of the total number of 1603 redundant workers. personnel services are to be provided to redundant workers, consisting of seven types of measures vocational guidance and other preparatory measures, employment and business services, vocational training, wage subsidies, business start-up grants, business support and services for new entrepreneurs and travel, accommodation and relocation allowances.
in writing. ‒ finland, in its application for funding, pointed to the difficult situation of workers in the ict sector, who are facing difficulties in finding their jobs during the economic crisis and the current global trend. the programme will help them find their way to success in today's labour market through a personal approach. the project will be co-financed by the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf).

in writing. ‒ i did not support the report on the request to mobilise the globalisation adjustment fund submitted by computer programming, finland. although i think that people who have lost their jobs as a result of globalisation changes in world trade need to be helped, not to mention situations where we have hundreds of workers laid off, the globalisation adjustment fund is not, in my view, the right instrument. while the fund itself provides funding for active measures to help redundant workers find employment, there are no thorough analyses of the impact of the fund's assistance that would produce sufficient comparative results and, where they exist, show that the success of the fund, and thus the success of redundant workers in finding new employment, varies from 4% to 86%, with the conclusions indicating that the workers who are most likely to find employment are those who should not be covered by measures financed by the fund. conversely, workers with lower education, older age, or living in areas with limited employment opportunities are least likely to have a chance. i therefore think that the fund does not generate enough added value and that with the funds currently being spent on the fund we could find more effective solutions for the redundant workers.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved the council's first reading position on the reform of eu trade mark law. the community trade mark reform also adopts the terminology of the treaty of lisbon, replacing the term 'community trade mark' with 'european union trade mark'. the most important part of the reform is the directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks, which aims to simplify and make cheaper and more accessible administrative procedures and trade mark registration. the eu expects the amendments to have a positive impact on economic growth and to increase the appetite for innovation. i voted in favour of parliament's adoption of the council's position.
in writing. ‒ the community trade mark regulation 207/2009 is the only existing legal instrument on intellectual property rights that is governed at european union level. the main objective of this proposal is to promote innovation and economic growth by making trade mark registration systems across the eu more accessible and efficient. the revision of the regulation aims to adapt terminology, simplify the procedures relating to the registration of a european trade mark, increase legal certainty of the rules, and create an appropriate framework for cooperation between ohim and the national offices for the development of common instruments. this system is already functioning, but with the current modernisation it should work more efficiently and better. the trade mark package is a key legal instrument to combat counterfeiting of products. our priorities are to preserve public health, safety and jobs, and to defend fundamental rights. the european parliament also achieved lower fees of up to 37%, less red tape, more efficiency and a system that benefits trademark users.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 207/2009 on the community trade mark. i also support the promotion of innovation and economic growth by making it easier and more efficient for businesses to access trade mark systems in europe, through cost reduction and complexity reduction, faster procedures, greater legal certainty and better protection against counterfeiting.
in writing. ‒ i approve the agreement reached between the council and the ep on the adaptation of the european trade mark. the main objective of this proposal is to promote innovation and economic growth by making the trade mark registration system more accessible and efficient. the amendment of this directive will adapt terminology, unify registration procedures and increase legal certainty by clarifying concepts. among other things, the name 'european union trade mark' is introduced and the office for these matters is renamed the european union intellectual property office. member states will also be able to set their fees in such a way as to guarantee the coexistence and complementarity between the european trade mark and the system of national trade marks. cooperation with national authorities is important in particular to bring the tools and presentation methods closer together. at national level, these adjustments should also improve the management structure of trade marks and speed up the application of administrative procedures. the system currently in place will be modernised and made more functional. the european trade mark package is a key tool in the fight against counterfeiting of products. at the same time, the financial and administrative costs of establishing a trade mark for the entrepreneur are reduced. so i believe that this system will become more accessible to its users.
in writing. ‒ the promoting the proper functioning of the single market is one of the eu's priorities. in a globalised world, brands are becoming increasingly important. of course, their protection is also important. it is important for an effective single market to provide businesses with uniform protection throughout the eu.
in writing. ‒ the second legal instrument adopted in the context of community or eu trade mark reform is a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks. through the second part of the reform, the regulation on community trade marks, and the said harmonisation directive, the eu legislator is supporting european innovation and economic growth. the directive will make trade mark provisions more transparent, increasing legal certainty. the directive also aims to approximate the substantive law and procedures governing trade marks in the member states, thereby facilitating their harmonisation with the eu trade mark system. the simplified cooperation between the trade mark offices of the member states and the european union office for harmonisation and internal market, which is envisaged by the directive, will also contribute to the more efficient functioning of the internal market. the reforms have enabled european smes to do their jobs more cheaply and simply, with a better legal and administrative framework. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the revised directive is designed to complement the so-called european union trade mark regulation by harmonising national trade mark rules. it is part of the same package as the regulation and they were negotiated together. for the purpose of harmonising the national trade mark systems of the european union, the provisions of the european union trade marks will also apply to national trade marks, thus bringing the regulation into line with the directive and approximating the trade mark laws of the member states. the main objective of the proposal is to promote innovation and economic growth.
in writing. ‒ i supported the directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks, because i am convinced that unification on this issue will help to improve the comprehensibility of trade marks across the european union. this amendment to the directive introduces a number of improvements aimed at increasing legal certainty and clarifying the scope of the lawful use of the member states' trade marks. the system at national level will thus bring the method of awarding the european trade mark closer together and facilitate the communication between the european and national authorising offices. this should make it easier to register and protect trade marks in all member states. the conditions under which an applicant may register a mark will also be more clear. the directive gives examples of signs which may be regarded as trade marks and also mentions clear grounds for refusing or invalidating a registration. on the other hand, the member state retains the right to decide whether to initiate a refusal of registration investigation. the new law will also allow trademarks to be used for trade names. these and other measures are also necessary to make european products and businesses more competitive vis-à-vis third countries.
in writing. ‒ the modernisation of the trade mark legislation aims to improve cooperation between national offices and the central european trade mark office. more efficient work between these institutions will contribute to better conditions within the european single market.

in writing. ‒ we have liberalised trade between the european union and the western balkan countries through a number of stabilisation and association agreements. in the case of bosnia and herzegovina, through the interim agreement and kosovo, as well as the region as a whole, agreements result from autonomous measures. the european commission's assessment of the proposal led to three major changes to the basic regulation (ec 1215/2009). these include, in particular, the extension of the current preferences until the end of 2020, the introduction of a human rights clause in the autonomous trade measures regulation and the possible suspension of the autonomous trade measures for bosnia and herzegovina as from 1 january 2016. the last point concerns in particular the fact that no agreement has been reached with bosnia and herzegovina on an interim agreement taking into account preferential traditional trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina.
in writing. ‒ the eu is liberalising trade with the western balkan countries through stabilisation and association agreements and, in the case of bosnia and herzegovina, through an interim agreement. since 2000, the eu has also granted these countries unilateral preferences that allow unrestricted duty-free access to the eu for most products. the commission proposal provides for three amendments to basic regulation (ec) no 1215/2009: the extension of the current preferences until the end of 2020. introduction of a so-called human rights clause in the autonomous trade measures regulation, which allows for the suspension of preferences in the event of a serious and systematic breach by a recipient country of the fundamental principles of human rights, democracy and the rule of law, possible suspension of the autonomous trade measures for bosnia and herzegovina from 1 january 2016 in relation to that country's disagreement with the modification of the interim agreement to take into account the preferential traditional trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina under the central european free trade agreement (cefta), which linked the two countries until 1 july 2013.
in writing. ‒ trade between the eu and the western balkan countries has been liberalised through several stabilisation and association agreements and, in the case of bosnia and herzegovina, through an interim agreement. in addition, the entire western balkan region benefits from the autonomous trade measures that the eu has granted since 2000. these unilateral preferences allow unrestricted duty-free access to the eu for most products. in the proposal under examination, the commission proposed three main amendments to the basic regulation. the first concerns the extension of the current preferences until the end of 2020, the second the introduction of the so-called human rights clause in the autonomous trade measures regulation and the third concerns the possible suspension of the autonomous trade measures for bosnia and herzegovina as of 1 january 2016. at present, negotiations with bosnia and herzegovina have not resulted in any agreement, and therefore a number of conditions for entitlement to preferential agreements are defined for it, such as respect for the definition of 'originating products', the obligation of recipient countries to refrain from introducing new duties or charges with regard to products originating in the eu, and the prevention of risks of fraud in trade relations.
in writing. ‒ countries participating in the process of stabilisation and integration into european structures must demonstrate in the accession processes their respect for the principles of democracy, the rule of law, the protection of human rights and minorities. but if there is a serious and systematic breach of these rules, the eu is forced to take action and define certain limits.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as i support all trade liberalisation initiatives.
in writing. ‒ the position adopted by parliament confirms the eu's determination to increase pressure on bosnia and herzegovina, which makes its willingness to agree to reciprocal trade with croatia conditional on further eu concessions. the adopted resolution is a warning to bosnia and herzegovina that its stubborn stance may lead not to greater concessions but, on the contrary, to the suspension of preferential trade measures by the eu. it is a strong signal to the government of this balkan country that the eu does support its integration into its territory, but only if it respects the rules and agreements in force.
