in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 6 november 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of ireland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by pwa international ltd operating in nace rev. 2 division 33 (machinery, equipment, equipment repair, commissioning) and the reintegration into the labour market of 108 young people not in employment, education or training (neets). the irish authorities claim that the redundancies at pwa international were caused by the closure of pwai following the company's decision to consolidate its north american and asian operations due to the trend towards deploying mro activities alongside global aviation hubs and the negative effects of the world trade agreements. the commission has found that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf and has therefore been approved by the ep today, which i voted in favour of. an important element of the application is that 108 young people not in employment, education or training, who were under 25 years of age at the time of the application, will also have access to personalised services co-financed by the egf.
in writing. ‒ the having regard to the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 between the european parliament, the council and the european commission on budgetary discipline and in the light of the council regulation as well as the regulation of the european parliament and of the council, i support the allocation of a financial contribution of eur 442 293 to ireland. this particular request concerns 108 redundant employees of pwa international ltd. the existing difficult situation in the area, together with the cumulative impact of the closure of three significant companies in the sgei sector in a short period of time and the fact that there are no employers left in the sector in ireland, could justify an exemption from the threshold of 500 redundancies set out in article 4 (1) of the egf regulation.
in writing. ‒ ireland submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf following the redundancies of 108 employees in pwa international ltd, a company in the machinery repair and installation sector, namely in the aerospace engineering sector, which has been affected by the global economic crisis. this is the lowest number of redundancies for which the egf is to be mobilised to date. the request is based on the exceptional circumstances in ireland where three significant businesses in the same sector closed and were made redundant in a short period of time. i therefore supported the ep resolution to provide ireland with support for personalised services for the unemployed and the integration of 108 people into the labour market for a total of eur 442 293.
in writing. ‒ ireland applied for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the redundancies in the service and general repair sector, in which ireland specialised at the end of the last century. the redundancies are due to the trend of the service and general repair activities being located close to the growing global air transport hubs, which are mainly located in north america and asia. another reason is the adverse effects of global trade agreements. the commission, after examining the application, has declared that the country fulfils all the conditions for the granting of a financial contribution. i therefore vote to mobilise the fund.
in writing. ‒ the eu has created legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers who are feeling the effects of major structural changes in the world trade pattern or the global financial and economic crisis and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is intended to help them do this. ireland has applied for a contribution from this fund of eur 442 293 to assist 108 redundant workers made redundant in a company which repaired and installed machinery and equipment. support should be directed to career guidance and planning and development, grants and training, training and further education programmes and programmes in the field of higher education. as these measures constitute active labour market measures, the commission and the ep supported ireland's request and, by resolution, supported the use of financial support from the european globalisation adjustment fund amounting to eur 442 293. i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ as the union has created this legislative and budgetary instrument with the intention of providing additional support to workers to help them reintegrate, i support this reasoned request by ireland.
in writing. - i voted against the motion. the european globalisation adjustment fund, by redistributing taxpayers' money, reduces the eu's competitiveness, thus exacerbating the very problem it is intended to tackle.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that we need a register of invasive alien species that are a threat to the union, as the protection of the health of our citizens must be a priority. we need to demand a list that is not political but scientific, up-to-date and capable of minimising the damage to human health caused by invasive alien species. the union list is directly applicable in all member states and it is therefore important that it complies with the requirements referred to above. in slovakia, for example, nearly half a million people are allergic to the pollen of the poppy, yet it took considerable effort to pass a law mandating eradication.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed an implementing regulation to adopt a list of invasive alien species of union concern. this concerns plant and mammal species that were not originally present in europe and that now pose a risk due to their adverse impact on biodiversity, ecosystem services, but also on human health and the economy. as the list presented by the commission is motivated mainly by the political will of the member states and does not take into account scientific criteria, i agree with the resolution of the parliament calling for the withdrawal of this proposal. moreover, the ep was not sufficiently informed about the way in which the risks would be assessed. according to the information available, many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not included in the list, and instead species that have no demonstrable negative impact on biodiversity or human health are included. for these reasons, the commission should withdraw its proposal and, after a thorough examination, submit a new, revised version.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as i agree with the objection that the list presented is inadequate.

in writing. ‒ the according to a study commissioned by the ep, the eu loses €50-70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance through profit shifting. this figure rises to eur 16 190 billion when account is taken of special tax regimes, tax collection shortcomings and other elements. such practices are unacceptable because in complex economic crises all economic actors must contribute on an equitable basis. if some multinationals do not contribute, unequal conditions arise under which, in particular, small and medium-sized enterprises cannot compete and are forced to lay off workers or to limit production and the provision of services. this results in lower tax bases and also less funding for national governments and a reduction in public services. in order to combat aggressive tax planning, member states must act in a coordinated manner while respecting the principle of the sovereignty of the member states. for this reason, there must be legislative measures within the eu to improve transparency, coordination and convergence in tax policies in the union. that's why i supported the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the in order to develop positive relations between the eu and china, it is necessary that they respect each other as strategic partners, not as rivals. the eu is china's largest trading partner, while china is the eu's second largest trading partner. it is necessary to develop mutually beneficial trade relations, to promote investment and tourism development, to address environmental improvement, cyber and computer security, as well as global and regional security issues, through economic and political dialogue and in compliance with applicable regulations and international agreements. it is also a path to enhance the promotion, respect and observance of human rights and the rule of law in china. eu member states need to focus more on china's rapid economic development and seize its opportunities.

in writing. ‒ following recent events, there is no doubt that the world is facing a humanitarian crisis of unprecedented scale, scope and persistence. although there has been a significant increase in funding recently, the need for humanitarian aid is growing much faster. in the future, security risks may increase as the perception of humanitarian aid as a tool used for political or economic reasons becomes more widespread. as a leading donor and a key global player in humanitarian action, the european union must take a leading role in seeking more effective and efficient ways to meet the needs of people affected by conflict and disaster. the world humanitarian summit next year should therefore focus on the special protection of women, children and people with disabilities. specific protection should be provided to children, in particular to facilitate their access to education during emergencies. we must work together to increase the involvement and cooperation of the private sector, ngos, local authorities and international organisations in humanitarian action and building partnerships with non-traditional donors. the european union must take the lead and play a key role in the whs process towards a strong outcome.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the largest donor and supporter of humanitarian action. humanitarian aid is based on four principles, also enshrined in the lisbon treaty: humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. it should therefore be provided to people who really need it, regardless of any external or internal factors of the country in which they live. the number of people in need of humanitarian assistance has multiplied in recent years, affected by internal and regional conflicts in countries as well as natural disasters. the situation is further complicated by the fact that some countries do not respect international humanitarian law and thus make it impossible to provide aid. the humanitarian aid regulation was adopted in 1996 and it is logical that in its 20 years of existence it no longer reflects the changing situation in the world. it is therefore necessary to revise and adapt it to new conditions so that the delivery of aid is coordinated and effective in the interests of those who need and rely on humanitarian aid.
in writing. ‒ the in the context of the report on the preparation of the world humanitarian summit: challenges and opportunities in the field of humanitarian aid, i consider it important to underline the paradox of the european union's position that, at a time when the world is facing humanitarian crises that are unprecedented in terms of the number of victims, it proposes to increase the number of unborn children by calling for easier access to abortion. instead of providing the necessary funds to facilities and institutions that save lives, the union wants to support with millions the organizations that perform and promote abortions in developing countries, and thus kill people, even though this is against the needs declared by the women themselves in these countries. recently, for example, on the floor of the european parliament, the zambian ambassador to belgium expressed the wish that development aid should really go to help mothers and children. in fact, in several third world countries, improvements in health care and overall living conditions have led to a decline in maternal mortality. but pro-abortion organizations want to attribute this fact artificially to the worldwide increase in abortions.
in writing. ‒ the number of people in need has more than doubled since 2004, to over 100 million in 2015. up to 250 million people are affected by humanitarian crises and, as a result of forced displacement, there are now more refugees and internally displaced persons than since the second world war. these are just a few of the facts in the report that have made me think more seriously about this question. it worries me that all events, such as natural disasters, the effects of climate change, military conflicts, epidemics, and population migration, most often affect the poor and marginalized, not excluding children. i supported the resolution because i am convinced that new solutions must be found and measures taken to make the world's humanitarian response more effective, which has been severely tested in recent years not only by the various natural disasters but also by the ongoing military conflicts and their consequences. in the context of humanitarian aid, i would like to highlight the work of humanitarian workers who, despite repeated attacks on their persons, provide basic care to the affected people and the affected regions in critical situations.
